Storybook fixture file for the full `UserPopout` experience, preloading chat store state, user profile query data, badges, and example messages. Search here for the canonical Twitch popout story, reply-eligibility variants, and how the popout is wired up in a centered Storybook wrapper.

Main chat user profile popout for Twitch and Kick, combining identity/profile data, recent messages, badges, channel links, reply/copy actions, moderation controls, and reconnect locking. Exports UserPopout plus public action and prop types used by the provider and chat surfaces.

Storybook coverage for the legacy footer wrapper around user-popout moderation actions. Search this file for timeout-dialog interaction tests, Kick/Twitch permutations, and the older footer-only rendering path kept for compatibility.

Compatibility wrapper that renders the state-aware timeout action and an external profile button for the user popout footer. Exports `UserPopoutFooter`, preserving older call sites while delegating moderation behavior to `StateAwareTimeoutAction` and `window.electronAPI.openExternal`.

Context provider and dispatcher for opening one shared UserPopout instance from chat usernames, including payload routing, focus restoration, provider remounting between users, and deferred reply/copy/channel actions. Exports UserPopoutProvider, useOpenUserPopout, and payload/action context types for chat integration and test-safe no-op behavior.

Storybook fixture for `UserProfileHeader` that documents the loaded and unavailable states of the user profile header UI. It provides a centered dark preview with mocked identity, account-created, and follow data plus retry handlers, making it easy to find the component’s visual states and stateful props.

Renders the chat user profile popout header with avatar, identity, account creation date, follow status, reconnect/retry states, and platform badges for Twitch or Kick. Includes accessible tooltips, date formatting, fallback avatars, and loading/error handling for profile fields.

React Query hook that loads Twitch/Kick user identity, account-created, follow, and channel-resolution data for the user popout. It exports the `useUserProfile` hook plus the render-state types and retry callbacks, and it translates IPC results into the profile/header states that the popout UI consumes.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/Moderat.summary: Storybook stories for `ModerationActionHighlightCompact`, covering timeout and ban examples with mocked deleted-message content. Useful for finding the compact moderation highlight card, its summary copy, and the shape of the props expected by the chat moderation UI.

Compact moderation event card that wraps `ChatEventHighlightCard` to show timeout/ban actions, deleted-message counts, and optional deleted-message previews. It is the streamlined chat moderation summary component used to surface enforcement actions with a red accent, icon, and test id for the moderation event highlight.

Storybook fixture for `ModerationActionHighlightCozy`, showing the moderation highlight card with timeout and ban variants, deleted-message preview content, and the summary text used to render chat moderation events. Useful when searching for Storybook coverage of moderation UI, delete-message layouts, or the `ChatHighlightCard`-based highlight pattern.

Memoized chat highlight component for moderation actions like timeout and ban, wrapping `ChatHighlightCard` with a red border, ban icon, summary block, and optional deleted-message section. This is the place to find the moderation-event presentation logic and the `deletedMessageCount`/`deletedMessages` render path.

Storybook stories for `ModeratorHighlight`, covering Twitch and Kick moderator callouts with sample message content. Use this file to find example platform-specific highlight rendering and the `ChatHighlightCard` story setup for moderator chat messages.

Memoized highlight component for moderator messages that renders a platform-specific icon for Twitch or Kick and delegates the card chrome to `ChatHighlightCard`. Search here for the moderator badge/highlight pattern and the `ChatPlatform`-driven icon switching logic.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/officia.summary: Hook and helpers for loading official emote images with per-URL success caching and a 7TV IPv4 fallback host when the primary CDN fails. Key exports are `getSevenTvIpv4FallbackUrl` and `useOfficialEmoteImageSource`, which fit into emote/image rendering to make source selection resilient across network edge cases.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/PinnedM.summary: Storybook stories for `PinnedMessageBanner`, seeded with chat fixtures and covered in viewer, moderator, busy, and expanded states. This file is the lookup point for pinned-message banner examples, interaction callbacks, and role-based banner behavior in Storybook.

Provides the shared pinned-message card for Twitch and Kick chats, including collapsed/expanded content, viewer dismissal versus moderator unpin actions, badge and emote rendering, and Twitch pin expiry progress. Contains pin-duration parsing, custom duration controls, countdown formatting, and responsive narrow-chat layout logic.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/Predict.summary: Storybook stories for `PredictionBanner`, seeded with Twitch and Kick prediction fixtures plus locked, resolved, and unified-style variants. Use this file to find how prediction banners are demonstrated in different states and how the story data is initialized from chat fixtures.

Read-only prediction banner for the chat viewer that mirrors Twitch/Kick community prediction cards, including collapsed/expanded states, countdown timing, auto-dismiss after resolution, and platform-specific styling. Exports `PredictionBanner` plus internal collapsed/active/ended UI helpers for showing prediction outcomes, lock status, and the viewer’s selected outcome without enabling voting.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/RaidHig.summary: Storybook coverage for `RaidHighlight`, showing the chat event highlight card used to render raid announcements in Twitch/Kick-style chat. Useful for finding the raid highlight component demo and its platform variants.

Memoized chat highlight wrapper for raid events that renders a `ChatEventHighlightCard` with a blue users icon, raid label, and platform-aware styling. Used as the raid-specific entry point in the chat highlights system.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/ResubHi.summary: Storybook examples for `ResubHighlight`, the resubscription chat event card. Shows the default Twitch-like presentation and helps developers find the resub highlight component and its visual variants.

Memoized chat event component for subscription resubs, built on `ChatEventHighlightCard` with an orange repeat icon and `Resub` label. This is the reusable UI hook for rendering recurring subscription milestones in chat.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/RitualH.summary: Storybook fixture for `RitualHighlight`, documenting the first-time chat ritual highlight card. Useful for locating the ritual milestone component and checking how it renders in chat.

Memoized highlight card for ritual or first-time chat events, implemented as a thin wrapper around `ChatEventHighlightCard` with a crown icon and pink accent. Serves as the ritual-specific renderer in the chat highlight pipeline.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/Subscri.summary: Storybook stories for `SubscriptionHighlight`, covering the subscription milestone card in Twitch and Kick contexts. Acts as the discoverability point for the subscription highlight UI and its platform-specific presentation.

Memoized subscription milestone component that wraps `ChatEventHighlightCard` with a gold star icon, accent bar, and `Subscription` label. Used to render new-sub and tiered subscription events consistently across chat platforms.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/tooltip.summary: Storybook scenarios for `BadgeTooltip`, including visible and hidden states with synthetic pointer positioning. Helps developers find the badge tooltip behavior, fullscreen positioning, and badge metadata rendering.

Portal-based badge tooltip that measures itself and positions near the mouse while avoiding viewport edges, then renders badge art, platform, and creator info. This is the hover tooltip implementation for chat badges and is optimized for fixed-position overlay behavior.

Storybook stories for `EmoteTooltip`, demonstrating the emote hover card with synthetic pointer coordinates and hidden state. Useful when searching for the emote tooltip preview and its animated display behavior.

Portal-based hover tooltip for chat emotes that measures mouse position and viewport bounds to keep the popover on-screen. Renders the emote preview, provider badge, author/date metadata, and GIF/ZW flags, making it the lookup target for emote hover UI, tooltip positioning, and provider branding.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/twitch/.summary: Shows a development-only banner when a moderation fixture is selected through the URL query string. Helps developers launch and test moderation states by selecting a real chat user without affecting normal production chat UI.

Seeds Twitch chat with recent historical messages fetched from recent-messages.robotty.de before the live IRC stream begins. Exports seedTwitchChatHistory, which respects chat display preferences, parses PRIVMSG and USERNOTICE lines, resolves badges, timestamps historical messages, caps the result, and prepends it to the chat store with best-effort failure handling.

Storybook entry for the production Twitch chat shell with mocked orchestrator dependencies and a fixed channel fixture. Use this file to find the isolated TwitchChat visual test harness, centered preview layout, and deterministic story setup.

Full Twitch chat panel coordinating live connection state, message ingestion, emotes and cosmetics, predictions, pinned messages, raids, chat modes, moderation actions, mod logs, and settings synchronization. Exports the main TwitchChat component used to render and operate a Twitch channel chat room.

Storybook cases for the Twitch pin-message modal, covering the default 30-minute flow, custom duration entry, and busy/loading state. Useful when searching for dialog interaction tests, Storybook play functions, and pin-duration UX fixtures.

Presentation-only Twitch modals for choosing how long a chat message stays pinned, with preset durations, custom seconds/minutes input, and no-expiry support. Exports `TwitchPinMessageDialog` and helper fragment-rendering logic, and it fits into the chat moderation flow by returning a duration to the parent `TwitchChat` component.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/Usernam.summary: Storybook fixtures for the chat username component, showing Twitch, Kick, and attached-suffix variants. Useful for finding username color, click behavior, and inline punctuation rendering in chat message layouts.

Reusable chat username renderer that resolves readable and theme-adapted colors, applies optional 7TV username paints, and opens channel-aware user popouts on interaction. Exports UsernameChannelContext and the Username component used across chat messages, replay views, and attribution rows.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat-replay/.summary: Storybook coverage for the chat replay rail, including populated, empty, drawer, and collapsed states plus a play interaction that clicks the collapse control. Helpful when searching for archived-video chat replay UI, seekable timeline behavior, and compact rail/drawer presentation.

Chat Replay side rail or drawer that displays archived messages synchronized to video playback, supports seeking, auto-scroll, historical browsing, collapse/close controls, rich links and mentions, badges, emotes, and platform-safe images. Exports ChatReplayRail for replay layouts.

Storybook scenarios for the `ChatReplaySession` container, covering desktop ready/loading/error/empty states and the compact drawer interaction on narrow widths. It seeds a playback store and stubs the Electron chat replay API so developers can find UI behavior, responsive layout, and loading/error handling in isolation.

Responsive controller for the Chat Replay feature that switches between a desktop rail and a mobile drawer, subscribes to playback state, fetches replay data through `useChatReplay`, and renders loading/error/supported views. It also handles retry, drawer open/close state, and hides unsupported replay entirely, making it the main orchestration layer for the chat replay sidebar.

Shared Storybook fixtures for chat replay tests and stories, including sample archived messages with offsets, badges, emotes, mentions, and links. It exports supported and empty `ChatReplayWindowResult` objects so developers can quickly find canonical replay data shapes and realistic message content for previews.

apps/desktop/src/components/dev/ChatSimT.summary: Storybook entry for the developer chat simulator tool, wrapping `ChatSimTool` in a constrained scrollable panel and seeding chat subsystem story stores first. It provides Twitch and Kick control variants so developers can locate a compact test harness for chat input and platform-specific controls.

Developer chat-event simulator for the desktop app, used to inject synthetic Twitch/Kick messages and moderation scenarios so engineers can verify chat rendering for bans, first-time chatter highlights, subscriptions, raids, mentions, and pinned/poll behavior. The main export is `ChatSimTool`, which writes most test events through `useChatStore.addMessage` and uses Kick chat service emitters for Kick-specific pinned content.

apps/desktop/src/components/dev/DebugPan.summary: Storybook fixture for the dev-only `DebugPanel`, intended to showcase the floating diagnostics widget in a fullscreen layout with seeded chat state. It exists as a developer preview/debug story and demonstrates the panel's DEV-only behavior rather than production UI.

Development-only draggable debug widget that hosts performance, chat simulation, and UI debugging tools. Exports DebugPanel, persists position, collapsed/hidden state, and active tool in localStorage, and supports keyboard toggling and viewport clamping.

apps/desktop/src/components/dev/interval.summary: Development-only `setInterval`/`clearInterval` shim that tracks live timers so the performance overlay can surface interval leaks and missing cleanup in effects. It exports `installIntervalTracker` to monkey-patch the browser timers once at app boot and `getActiveIntervalCount` for inspection.

apps/desktop/src/components/dev/PerfTool.summary: Storybook story for the internal `PerfTool` developer panel, wrapped in seeded chat-store fixtures so performance diagnostics can render in a realistic app state. The file exports a simple `Dashboard` story and is mainly used to test the performance tool UI in isolation.

apps/desktop/src/components/discovery/ca.summary: Filter controls for category discovery pages, combining language selection, tag search, and optional viewer-count sorting. Normalizes the Radix Select all-languages sentinel and keeps local tag input synchronized with the parent query state.

Storybook stories for the responsive `CategoryGrid` component, covering populated, loading, empty, and compact layouts. Useful for finding the component's presentational API, fixture data usage, and how the grid behaves under different states.

Responsive category listing grid that renders `CategoryCard` items, loading skeletons, or an empty-state message based on `categories` and `isLoading`. Exports `CategoryGrid` and fits as the simple non-virtualized view used by the discovery screen for small to medium result sets.

apps/desktop/src/components/discovery/vi.summary: Storybook stories for the windowed `VirtualizedCategoryGrid`, showing populated, loading, next-page fetching, and empty states. Helps developers inspect virtualization behavior, infinite-scroll affordances, and large-dataset rendering in isolation.

Performance-focused virtualized grid for rendering large category datasets with responsive column counts, overscan, progressive reveal, loading skeletons, and infinite-scroll loading. Tracks dataset generations to invalidate stale reveal callbacks and optionally restores scroll position through sessionStorage.

apps/desktop/src/components/icons/index..summary: Barrel export for platform icon components, re-exporting the icon set from `PlatformIcons`. Use this entry point when searching for platform-brand SVGs or the shared icon API instead of importing individual files directly.

apps/desktop/src/components/icons/Platfo.summary: Storybook showcase for the platform brand icons, including Twitch, Kick, 7TV, and Kick emote variants. Useful for checking sizing, color treatment, and how the icons are intended to be used as contextual brand marks rather than general UI accents.

SVG icon component set for platform branding, exporting `TwitchIcon`, `KickIcon`, `SevenTVIcon`, and `KickEmoteIcon`. These components provide consistent brand marks with configurable size/className props and are used anywhere the app needs platform identification or emote-picker branding.

apps/desktop/src/components/multistream/.summary: Top-level multistream layout controller that renders the stream grid, focus-mode side rail, and empty-state messaging. Exports `MultiStreamGrid` and wires drag-and-drop reordering, keyboard focus shortcuts (`Ctrl+1..6`), slot focus promotion via `electronAPI`, and store-driven mute/focus state from `useMultiStreamStore`.

Defines reusable Storybook fixtures for multistream layouts, channels, live streams, and favorite references, plus mocked Electron API handlers and a store-reset helper. Provides deterministic Twitch/Kick data for testing add-stream flows, favorites, playback failures, channel search, and capacity states.

Storybook entry for the draggable multistream slot wrapper, showing the `SortableStreamSlot` inside a `DndContext` and `SortableContext`. Uses shared multistream mocks and store reset helpers to verify drag-handle wiring, slot chrome, and sortable behavior in isolation.

Thin drag-and-drop adapter around `StreamSlot` that uses `useSortable` from `@dnd-kit/sortable` to attach drag listeners, transform styles, and accessibility attributes. Exports `SortableStreamSlot`, which is used by the grid layout when streams are in reorderable grid mode.

Storybook stories for the core stream tile component, covering offline fallback, focused Kick layout, staggered lazy loading, and custom drag-handle props. This file helps developers find visual states for `StreamSlot` without running the full multistream pipeline.

Core stream tile renderer for multistream, responsible for loading playback, showing channel metadata, handling mute/chat/focus controls, and coordinating WCV/legacy player paths. Exports `StreamSlot` and fits into the multistream grid as the unit that mounts Twitch or Kick players, defers startup with staggered/lazy loading, and talks to `useMultiStreamStore` plus Electron slot IPC.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/AGENT.summary: Project guide for the desktop player component directory, explaining the HLS.js player stack, platform wrappers for Kick and Twitch, and where to find playback controls, quality logic, PiP, and lifecycle hooks. Useful when searching for player architecture, refactoring boundaries, watchdog behavior, or the source of quality, fullscreen, and live-stream handling.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/capti.summary: Storybook fixtures for `CaptionErrorNotice`, covering the recoverable caption failure UI and the hidden/null state. Use this to find the visual test cases for retryable timed-text errors and the component's placement above player controls.

Small overlay notice that displays a caption loading failure with a retry action, returning `null` when there is no timed-text error. This is the component to find for recoverable subtitle/caption errors, retry flows, and the accessibility status announcement around caption recovery.

Storybook scenarios for `CaptionOverlay`, including standard cues, positioned WebVTT-style cues, empty state, and local live word-highlighting. Useful for finding examples of subtitle positioning, cue layout rules, and local caption highlight behavior in the player UI.

Caption rendering overlay for the video player, merging user caption preferences with cue layout logic for fallback and positioned subtitles. It handles WebVTT-style positioning, local live word highlighting, final-caption screen-reader announcements, and safe spacing above player controls.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/hls-b.summary: Pure config resolver that maps persisted buffer preferences into HLS.js live and VOD buffer settings, including live sync counts, max buffer caps, and byte-size scaling. Search here for the buffer policy layer between user preferences and `new Hls({...})`, especially live-latency limits and buffer-size clamping behavior.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/hls-p.summary: Storybook coverage for the raw `HlsPlayer` media engine, intentionally using inert sources so the catalog never hits a live HLS CDN. Useful for finding the lowest-level player entry point, native control variants, and the live-configuration story used to document engine behavior.

Reusable HLS.js-backed React video player for live streams and VOD, exposing quality selection, preferred-quality handling, volume, source changes, HLS instance access, and normalized playback errors. Includes live fragment watchdog/recovery, buffer configuration, memory cleanup, CDN detection, and decoder teardown to improve stream reliability and prevent renderer memory growth.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/hooks.summary: React hook that monitors network conditions and player buffer health to automatically pick a better or safer HLS quality tier. Exports `useAdaptiveQuality`, `AdaptiveQualityOptions`, and `AdaptiveQualityState`; it plugs into the player to handle network-aware quality downgrades, hysteresis, and auto-switching between `auto`, `high`, `medium`, and `low`.

React hook for throttling playback when the app is hidden or unfocused, using page visibility and window focus events plus a grace timer. Exports `useBackgroundThrottle`, `BackgroundThrottleOptions`, `BackgroundThrottleState`, and `ThrottleAction`; it coordinates pause, mute, or quality reduction behavior so background streams use fewer resources.

Hook that applies the authenticated user's default playback quality once HLS quality levels first become available, while avoiding overrides of later user selections. Exports useDefaultQuality and integrates quality preference resolution, auth state, and player logging.

Fullscreen state and toggle hook for the player container, wiring `fullscreenchange` events to local React state and exposing a safe `toggleFullscreen` callback. It handles the browser fullscreen API and logs failures through the renderer logger.

Development-only React hook that verifies decoded player audio can reach the local caption pipeline without recording or exposing PCM data. Binds LocalAudioCaptureController to a video element, reports capture state through dataset attributes and diagnostic proof strings, and logs non-silent RMS measurements.

React hook that orchestrates on-device live captions for a video stream using LocalAudioCaptureController and Electron local-caption events. Manages model readiness, persisted caption preferences, recognizer generations and result sequencing, media-clock resets, timed cue presentation, native TextTrack captions, mute/volume state, and cleanup.

Picture-in-picture hook for the player video element that tracks PiP entry/exit events and exposes a toggle callback using the browser PiP API. It keeps player UI state aligned with `document.pictureInPictureElement` and logs API failures.

Global keyboard shortcut hook for player controls, mapping keys to play/pause, mute, volume, fullscreen, theater mode, and seeking while ignoring form controls and interactive elements. Exports usePlayerKeyboard for reusable media-player keyboard interaction.

React hook that manages HTML video and HLS resource lifecycle, including preload configuration, lazy loading with IntersectionObserver, active-state pausing, source reset, cleanup, and experimental memory-pressure monitoring. Exports VideoLifecycleOptions, VideoLifecycleState, and useVideoLifecycle for player components.

Persistent volume hook that syncs a video element with the global volume store, handles mute toggles, forced-mute overrides, and suppresses HLS init races with a short guard window. Exports `useVolume`, which is used by player controls and playback components to keep UI state and the underlying media element aligned.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/kick/.summary: Kick player barrel file that re-exports the Kick-specific player variants for live streams and VOD playback. This is the main import surface for finding Kick-tuned components like `KickHlsPlayer`, `KickLivePlayer`, and `KickVodPlayer` without knowing their individual paths.

Custom HLS.js playlist loader for Kick clips that rewrites `.m3u8` media playlists by dropping the first segment and bumping media sequence numbers. Exports `isKickClipPlaylistUrl` and `createKickClipPlaylistLoader`, and solves the mid-GOP clip problem where HLS would otherwise initialize audio-only playback.

Small resolver that returns Kick-specific HLS config overrides when the source URL matches a Kick clip playlist. Exports `resolveKickHlsConfig`, which wires the custom playlist loader into the generic HLS player only for the problematic Kick clip case.

Storybook entry for `KickHlsPlayer` with safe fixture props and preview states like poster-only, live configuration, and native controls. Useful for finding the component’s visual contract and for testing the Kick-specific HLS wrapper in isolation without hitting production media.

Thin wrapper around the shared `HlsPlayer` that injects Kick-specific HLS config overrides based on the source URL. Exports `KickHlsPlayer`, the main component to use when rendering Kick streams that may need the custom clip loader.

Storybook fixtures for `KickLivePlayerControls`, covering paused, playing, loading, muted, and fullscreen states against a Kick-branded backdrop. Helps developers discover the live-control layout and interaction props without inspecting the implementation.

Kick-branded live player controls component that composes the generic `PlayerControls` with a green LIVE badge, optional Go Live action, and a Kick progress bar handle. Exports `KickLivePlayerControls`, used by the live player to present Kick-specific playback controls and live-edge behavior.

Storybook fixtures for the video telemetry overlay, feeding fake HLS and HTMLVideoElement data to show bitrate, latency, resolution, and dropped-frame stats. Helps developers find the diagnostics/debug overlay and its condition that nothing renders until both HLS and video objects exist.

Heads-up video diagnostics overlay for HLS playback in the Twitch player. It reads live stats from an `hls.js` instance and `<video>` element, computes buffer, bandwidth, codec, latency, FPS, and session IDs, and renders a closeable debug table for player troubleshooting.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/types.summary: Shared player domain types for quality levels, platform identifiers, stream playback formats, standardized playback errors, timed-text tracks and cues, and local live-caption metadata. Provides the contracts used by Twitch and Kick player components and HLS integrations.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/video.summary: Storybook scenarios for the main `VideoPlayer` component. It sets up centered preview shells and fixture args for Twitch, Kick, and theater-mode states so developers can visually test the player chrome without a real source stream.

Composable HLS video player for live streams and VOD playback, combining fullscreen, picture-in-picture, persistent volume, resume playback, keyboard shortcuts, seek previews, quality selection, buffering state, and custom controls. Exports VideoPlayer and coordinates HlsPlayer with PlayerControls and player hooks.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/volum.summary: Storybook variants for the reusable `VolumeControl` UI. Provides loud, quiet, muted, and zero-volume states inside a dark shell so the slider, tooltip, and mute icon behavior can be inspected in isolation.

Compact volume/mute control with hover-reveal slider, draggable thumb, and tooltip feedback. It reads player-control preferences from auth state, falls back to defaults, and leaves actual audio state to the parent via `onVolumeChange` and `onMuteToggle`.

apps/desktop/src/components/recording/re.summary: Storybook coverage for the recording completion notice shown after a capture finishes. It exercises completed, partial, failed, and TypeScript-fallback outcomes using recording fixtures so designers and developers can validate the in-app result banner states.

Provides pause, resume, and stop controls for an active stream recording session across global and player surfaces. RecordingPauseResumeControl manages recording-phase state, pending actions, accessible labels, focus restoration, and action feedback through stream recording hooks.

Storybook stories for the stop-recording dialog, covering the default trigger state and the confirmation flow when the stop button is clicked. It uses recording snapshot fixtures to mock the stream-recording provider and exercise the UI in isolation.

Stop-recording control with an alert dialog that lets users keep recording, finalize and save the captured stream, or permanently discard it. Uses stream recording state and actions, prevents duplicate submissions, handles fullscreen dialog mounting, and restores focus for accessible confirmation flows.

Storybook fixture helpers for stream recording UI, including factory functions for active recording snapshots and completed/partial/failed notices. It also patches the window electron bridge so recording components can render against deterministic mocked state and no-op actions.

apps/desktop/src/components/search/Unifi.summary: Storybook fixtures and interaction stories for the cross-platform UnifiedSearchInput component. Covers resting state, search history, channel/category results, live-only channel selection, platform filtering, and favorite actions using React Query test data.

Reusable React search input and dropdown for unified channel, category, and stream discovery across platforms. Combines debounced query hooks, search history, ranked channel matching, category routing, live-only filtering, favorites actions, infinite-scroll limits, and selectable navigation results.

apps/desktop/src/components/recording/re.summary: In-app toast/status notice for completed, partial, or failed stream recordings, with copy that adapts to TS fallback, output format, and error states. Exports `RecordingOutcomeNotice` and `RecordingOutcomeBridge`, and wires action buttons for opening the saved recording, showing it in the folder, or dismissing the notice through stream recording hooks.

Storybook fixtures for the persistent recording status pill shown in the app chrome, covering active, paused-with-gap, quality-changed, and custom control composition states. Uses recording snapshot helpers to exercise the `RecordingGlobalIndicator` UI in centered docs-friendly previews.

Top-level recording status indicator that shows the current stream recording phase, captured duration, and a dropdown-style details panel with session metadata and controls. Exports `RecordingGlobalIndicator`, which composes pause/resume and stop controls, handles outside-click/Escape dismissal, and links into the stream detail route.

Storybook scenarios for the recording recovery dialog, including interrupted sessions, finalize-only recovery, and dismissal confirmation behavior. Drives the dialog with snapshot state and interaction tests so developers can verify recovery flows without a live stream.

Alert dialog for recovering interrupted stream recordings. Lets users resume, finalize, or permanently dismiss saved recording segments while handling unavailable or changed streams, async action errors, confirmation flows, loading states, and keyboard focus restoration.

Storybook entries for the recording session control buttons, showing recording, paused, and resuming states with the `surface` prop set up for player or global chrome. Uses shared recording fixtures to document how `RecordingSessionControls` responds to different session phases.

apps/desktop/src/components/settings/Bug.summary: Storybook scenarios for the Settings bug-report panel, with Electron IPC mocks for listing reports, opening the reports folder, and writing a markdown report. Includes a play-based interaction test that types a description and verifies the generated report success state, which makes this file easy to find when searching for Storybook coverage, mock `window.electronAPI`, or bug-report UI tests.

Renderer-side Settings → Report a Bug panel that collects a reproduction description, toggles inclusion of main and noise logs, writes a markdown bug report through `window.electronAPI.bugReports`, and exposes copy/open-folder actions plus recent-report listing. Key exports are `BugReportSection`, and it fits the project as the UI layer for bug-report generation and log attachment with toast-based feedback and noise-log availability probing.

apps/desktop/src/components/settings/Cha.summary: Storybook stories for the chat settings surface, including grouped preference views and a reusable row-primitives example. It resets the auth store to default chat preferences, overrides selected chat-display values for one scenario, and helps developers find the reusable `SettingRow`, `SwitchRow`, and `RangeRow` patterns used by chat settings and quick-settings UI.

Settings UI and shared writer hook for chat display preferences, including appearance, emotes, events, and behavior controls. Handles optimistic updates, preference hydration, serialized persistence, defaults, and saved notifications for the Chat settings tab and in-chat quick settings.

apps/desktop/src/components/settings/Log.summary: Storybook coverage for the Logs settings panel, with mocked Electron log paths and tail output for populated, empty, and error states. The stories exercise log-file selection and network-log rendering, so developers searching for log viewer examples, `window.electronAPI.logs` mocks, or tail/error handling will land here.

Settings panel for tailing desktop app log files with live refresh, level/tag filtering, and a text/table toggle for diagnosing runtime and network activity. Exports `LogsSection` plus helpers for parsing project log lines, extracting network request rows, and building cURL commands from request metadata.

apps/desktop/src/components/stream/activ.summary: Storybook fixture for the active-recording blocking dialog, used to test the UX when a second live recording is requested. Shows open and closed states around `ActiveRecordingDialog`, with router and button wiring for focus-return behavior.

Modal dialog that prevents starting a second stream recording while one is already active, explaining the single-recording constraint and linking back to the current capture. Exports `ActiveRecordingDialog`, which wraps the shared dialog primitives and routes to the active recording page when a recording exists.

apps/desktop/src/components/stream/AGENT.summary: Developer-facing index for the `stream/` component subtree, explaining how stream cards, featured heroes, channel info, and related VOD/clip browsing fit together. Useful for finding the public exports, state ownership rules, routing conventions, and platform-specific patterns used across the stream browsing UI.

apps/desktop/src/components/stream/featu.summary: Storybook scenarios for the featured-stream hero component, covering single Twitch/Kick streams, multi-stream carousel behavior, loading, and empty states. Helps developers locate `FeaturedStream` and understand the homepage hero patterns and supported stream variants.

apps/desktop/src/components/stream/relat.summary: Implements a custom clip video player supporting HLS manifests through hls.js and native MP4/HLS playback, with recovery and error handling for stream failures. Exports playback controls for play/pause, seeking, persistent volume and mute state, fullscreen mode, control visibility, and loading progress.

Storybook cases for the related-content tab bar, wiring `ContentTabs` into a `RelatedContentStoryRouter` so designers and developers can preview the Home, Videos, and Clips states in isolation. Useful for finding the navigation tabs, router search-param behavior, and active-tab styling for the stream related-content UI.

Sticky tab navigation for the stream related-content page, rendering router links for Home, Videos, and Clips with active underline and muted/active text states driven by the `tab` search param. This is the navigation surface to search for when changing stream content sections or route-linked tab behavior.

Storybook fixtures for the full `RelatedContent` browser, mocking `window.electronAPI` responses to show success, empty, and error states across Home, Videos, and Clips. This file is the quickest place to find test doubles and preview data for the related-content data-fetching flow and dialog/card rendering.

Renders the stream page’s related-content dashboard with Home, Videos, and Clips tabs, sorting and time-range filters, pagination, clip playback dialogs, loading/error states, and live-to-offline refetch behavior. Coordinates VideoCard and ClipCard rendering with lazy mounting, image prewarming, localStorage preferences, router search state, and Electron API data fetching.

apps/desktop/src/components/stream/featu.summary: Renders the home page featured livestream hero with a rotating carousel of Twitch or Kick streams, thumbnails, live viewer counts, metadata, navigation, and muted preview playback. Integrates HLS players, persisted volume, ad-block state, routing, loading skeletons, and stream display utilities.

apps/desktop/src/components/stream/relat.summary: Storybook coverage for `ClipCard` with centered routing context and fixtures for default, long-title, and missing-artwork states. Use this file to find visual regressions around clip thumbnails, channel avatar fallback, and router-linked category behavior in related-content UI.

Memoized related-content card for stream clips and videos. Displays proxied thumbnails, duration, views, relative date, channel avatar, category routing, and hover playback affordances while minimizing parent-list re-renders.

Storybook scenarios for the clip modal/dialog, including Twitch embed fallback, loading state, Kick VOD lookup errors, and metadata-missing edge cases. Search this file when you need examples of how the clip viewer behaves across platform-specific playback and fallback conditions.

Provides the modal workflow for viewing a selected Twitch or Kick clip, including playback readiness and error states, channel metadata, follow/share/download actions, history tracking, and navigation to full VODs. Normalizes inconsistent clip metadata fields and coordinates platform-specific VOD players and Electron video lookup APIs.

Storybook harness for the `ClipPlayer` video component, with decorators that seed the global volume store and show paused and muted playback states. Use it to find clip player rendering, audio-state, and autoplay/volume integration examples.

Test fixture factory for the related-content stream UI, generating realistic Twitch VOD and clip records plus a sample channel object. Exports `relatedChannel`, `makeVideo`, `makeClip`, `relatedVideos`, and `relatedClips` for Storybook stories that need stable stream metadata, thumbnails, and clip/VOD routing cases.

In-memory TanStack Router wrapper for related-content story views. Defines stream, video, and category routes with platform/channel parameters, search validation, and configurable initial navigation while rendering supplied story children.

Defines the shared TypeScript contracts for related videos and clips, clip playback, and the RelatedContent component. Captures platform metadata, VOD/live state, channel details, stream tags, availability, URLs, and callback behavior used across related-content cards and players.

Provides formatting helpers for related-content metadata: converts ISO dates into relative time labels and numeric view counts into compact K/M notation. Used by video and clip cards to present human-readable timestamps and engagement metrics.

Storybook scenarios for the `VideoCard` component covering archived VODs, live streams, and subscriber-only states across Twitch and Kick. Uses the related-content story router plus fixture data to exercise routing, badges, and card presentation in a centered layout.

Displays a memoized video or live-stream card with thumbnail, duration/live status, views, date, channel avatar, category link, and subscription-only badges. Determines whether to route to a VOD or live channel page, passes playback and channel metadata through router search parameters, and hides cards whose proxied thumbnails fail.

Back-compat barrel that re-exports the modular `RelatedContent` component and its public types from the new folder structure. Exists to keep older imports working while the related-content feature is split into smaller files.

apps/desktop/src/components/stream/strea.summary: Storybook fixture for the `StreamCardSkeleton` loading state, showing the placeholder geometry in single-card and multi-row layouts. Useful for verifying loading shimmer spacing and card proportions before stream data arrives.

Minimal loading placeholder for a live stream card, preserving the thumbnail, avatar, title, category, and tag layout with skeleton blocks. Used wherever stream tiles need a consistent perceived-loading state before metadata is available.

Storybook coverage for the `StreamCard` live-stream tile, including normal, Kick, currently-watching, compact-metadata, and thumbnail-fallback cases. The stories rely on app-router wiring and catalog fixtures to exercise platform identity, verification, tags, and fallback rendering.

Memoized stream discovery card that displays live status, viewer count, platform branding, channel avatar, category, language, and tags, then links to the stream route. Uses debounced hover prefetching for channel and stream detail queries, with a startup grace period for Kick requests.

Storybook scenarios for the stream grid component, covering populated, currently-watching, loading, and empty states. Useful for finding the responsive stream collection UI and its loading skeleton/empty-state behavior in isolation.

Responsive grid for rendering stream cards with loading skeletons, empty-state messaging, active-stream highlighting, stable stream keys, and first-batch stagger animation. Used by browse and stream-list views to present UnifiedStream collections.

Storybook scenarios for StreamInfo covering live Twitch and Kick channels, offline metadata, loading state, and the authenticated channel-owner view. Uses catalog fixtures, router decorators, and temporary auth-store state to exercise verification, partner status, maturity, tags, uptime, follow-related, and ownership rendering.

Renders stream and channel metadata for Twitch and Kick pages, including avatars, verification, follower counts, titles, categories, language tags, live status, uptime, and recording actions. Handles loading skeletons, authenticated owner detection, cross-platform category links, and offline timing labels.

Storybook playground for the platform verification badge, showing Twitch and Kick variants plus size examples. This is the place to find the reusable verified-mark asset/markup used across stream cards and stream headers.

Platform-aware verified badge renderer for stream headers and channel identity UI. Uses the bundled Kick verified badge asset when available, otherwise falls back to an inline Twitch-style SVG badge; search for stream status badges, platform branding, or verified indicator components.

apps/desktop/src/components/ToastRoot.st.summary: Storybook coverage for the global toast viewport with success, error, warning, and info examples. Exercises the imperative Sonner API through a preview component so developers can find the shared notification shell, toast styling, and icon variants.

apps/desktop/src/components/ToastRoot.ts.summary: Single app-wide Sonner toaster mount that standardizes toast placement, dark styling, borders, icons, and timing. Centralizes imperative notifications for auth failures, moderation actions, and other global events so the whole renderer uses one consistent toast surface.

apps/desktop/src/components/TopNavBar/in.summary: Storybook scenarios for the top navigation bar under logged-out, logged-in, and collapsed-sidebar states. Seeds the app, auth, and notification stores to preview the full chrome, making it easy to find nav-state wiring, store dependencies, and authenticated header behavior.

Defines the main application navigation bar with StreamFusion branding, sidebar collapse control, global search, recording status, notifications, and profile actions. Uses selective app-store subscriptions and memoization to avoid unnecessary navigation re-renders.

apps/desktop/src/components/TopNavBar/No.summary: Storybook states for the notifications dropdown, including populated, empty, and unread-overflow cases. Seeds notification and follow stores plus auto-opens the menu so developers can inspect unread badges, relative times, and bulk notification actions.

Provides the live-notification bell dropdown for newly active channels, including unread counts, relative timestamps, platform avatars, stream navigation, mark-all-read, individual dismissal, and clearing all notifications. Integrates with the notification store and closes automatically when clicking outside.

apps/desktop/src/components/TopNavBar/Se.summary: Storybook coverage for the top-nav search field in default and narrow widths. Useful for finding the unified search entry point and checking responsive layout constraints around the header search surface.

Top-navigation search wrapper around the shared unified search input. Submitting a term navigates to the app search route with a `q` query param, so search for header search routing or unified search integration here.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/button.st.summary: Storybook coverage for the shared `Button` primitive, showing variant, size, disabled, busy, and `asChild` composition states. Useful when searching for button docs, Storybook controls, and visual examples of the StreamFusion action button patterns.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/button.ts.summary: Reusable `Button` component built on Radix `Slot` and `class-variance-authority`, with variant and size styling for default, secondary, outline, ghost, Twitch, Kick, destructive, and link actions. This is the project’s core action primitive, used anywhere developers need a typed, theme-aware button with `asChild` support.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/card.stor.summary: Storybook examples for the `Card` container, demonstrating default and dense layouts with header, content, footer, and inline action patterns. Search this file for card composition examples, surface styling, and how the desktop app presents grouped content blocks.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/card.tsx.summary: Primitive card layout components (`Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter`) implemented as simple styled wrappers. This file defines the reusable surface/container building blocks used for panels, grouped content, and tonal sectioning throughout the app.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/dialog.st.summary: Storybook stories for the modal `Dialog` pattern, including closed and default-open confirmation flows. Useful for finding dialog usage, portal behavior in Storybook, and the destructive confirmation UX wired to the shared dialog components.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/dialog.ts.summary: Wraps Radix UI Dialog primitives into styled, reusable modal components with animated overlays, centered content, accessible titles and descriptions, optional close buttons, and custom portal containers. Exports the complete dialog composition used throughout the desktop interface.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/follow-bu.summary: Storybook scenarios for the app-specific `FollowButton`, seeded with auth and follow store state to show Twitch, Kick, and already-following behavior. Search here for store-backed interaction examples, optimistic follow states, and platform-specific follow affordance docs.

Interactive follow/unfollow control for Twitch and Kick channels. Coordinates follow-store state, authenticated platform account actions, pending states, hover icons, platform styling, and error toasts for reconnect or failed follow changes.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/scroll-ar.summary: Radix-based scroll container with styled viewport, configurable vertical or horizontal scrollbar, thumb states, and corner handling. Exports ScrollArea for reusable overflow regions across the desktop UI.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/select.st.summary: Storybook coverage for the custom `Select` component, showing default, open, disabled, and unavailable-option states. Useful for finding examples of grouped dropdown content, portalled menus, and accessibility-oriented labeling patterns around the select API.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/select.ts.summary: Radix Select wrapper that provides the project’s styled dropdown control, including trigger, content portal, grouped labels, items, separators, and scroll buttons. Exports the full select building blocks for use in forms, filters, and menu-style choice pickers with consistent theming and keyboard behavior.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/skeleton..summary: Storybook examples for the `Skeleton` placeholder component, demonstrating simple placeholders and realistic loading layouts like stream cards and channel lists. Helps developers see how to reserve space during async loading to avoid layout shift.

Reusable animated loading placeholder component that applies theme-aware elevated background styling and respects reduced-motion preferences. Exports Skeleton for indicating pending content in UI layouts.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/switch.st.summary: Storybook stories for the `Switch` control, covering settings rows, on/off states, and disabled behavior. A good entry point for finding examples of labeled toggle rows and form-like preference panels in the desktop UI.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/switch.ts.summary: Radix Switch wrapper with custom track, thumb, and checkmark styling for binary settings. Exports `Switch` with an extra `thumbClassName` prop, and fits into preference screens, feature toggles, and other boolean controls.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/tooltip.s.summary: Storybook stories for the tooltip system, showing icon-button affordances, default hover behavior, open state, and grouped player controls. Useful for finding how the project documents short helper text that portals above the UI without disrupting keyboard users.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/tooltip.t.summary: Radix Tooltip wrapper that defines the shared provider, trigger, and styled content/arrow presentation for brief contextual help. Exports `Tooltip`, `TooltipTrigger`, `TooltipContent`, and `TooltipProvider`, and supports custom portal containers for embedding in different UI surfaces.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/visually-.summary: Storybook examples for `VisuallyHidden`, demonstrating accessible icon buttons and status text that should remain in the accessibility tree. Helps developers find patterns for screen-reader-only labels and supplementary semantics without changing layout.

Thin wrapper around Radix `VisuallyHidden` that exposes a reusable component for assistive-only text. Exports `VisuallyHidden`, which is used to add accessible labels and descriptions while keeping the visual design unchanged.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/browser-elect.summary: Proxy-based Electron API relay that forwards browser app calls through a client, while short-circuiting local window methods and fixture-backed playback responses. Exports `BrowserRelayClient` and `createBrowserElectronApi`, and plugs into dev playback, moderation fixtures, and user-profile fixtures for browser-electron integration testing.

apps/desktop/src/docs/twitch-player-fix-.summary: Postmortem-style resolution note for a Twitch HLS reinitialization bug that caused black screens or reloads when changing stream quality. Describes the `TwitchHlsPlayer` `useEffect` dependency fix, the new direct `currentLevel` update path, and the cleanup that removed debug instrumentation.

apps/desktop/src/global.css.summary: Global Tailwind CSS v4 theme and application styling for StreamFusion. Defines Twitch/Kick brand colors, dark UI semantic tokens, shadcn token mappings, typography, scrollbar and switch styles, reusable badges/cards, keyframe animations, staggered grid utilities, and root layout behavior.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/AGENTS.md.summary: Directory guide for reusable renderer React hooks, documenting auth, Electron IPC, chat synchronization, moderation, Twitch/Kick integrations, ad blocking, TanStack Query hooks, timers, persistence, and lifecycle contracts. Use it to find hook responsibilities, exports, invariants, cache behavior, and integration patterns before modifying hooks.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/chat-replay-playb.summary: In-memory external store for chat replay playback state, exposing a small pub/sub API around `VideoPlaybackSnapshot` plus seek events. It also exports `useChatReplayPlaybackSnapshot`, a `useSyncExternalStore` hook for keeping replay controls and timeline consumers in sync.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/chat-replay-windo.summary: Pure selector that filters chat replay messages to the visible time window based on the current playback position. This is the place to search for replay chat virtualization, lookback-window logic, and offset-based message slicing.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/index.ts.summary: Barrel file that re-exports the public hook surface for the desktop app, including auth, Electron integration, and updater hooks. Import from here when you want the canonical hook entrypoint instead of deep-linking into individual files.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/browser-entry.summary: Bootstraps the browser-side development relay entrypoint for the desktop app. It marks the window as a dev client, applies moderation fixtures from the query string, waits for a relay WebSocket, installs a browser `electronAPI` bridge, and then lazy-loads the renderer; this is the file to search for the browser relay startup path and dev-only Electron API wiring.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/codec.ts.summary: Encodes and decodes relay-safe values that need to cross the dev relay boundary without losing special JavaScript types. It exports `encodeRelayValue` and `decodeRelayValue` for `undefined`, `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, and `ArrayBuffer`/typed-array payloads, and is the serialization layer underneath the relay protocol.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/config.ts.summary: Builds the Vite/browser development config that enables the StreamFusion relay proxy only in dev serve mode. It exports `createBrowserDevelopmentConfig`, validates the relay port and token, and wires `__streamfusion-dev` to a localhost WebSocket proxy with the required auth header.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/host-bootstra.summary: Starts the host-side half of the development relay only when browser relay mode is enabled and the current runtime is not the browser client. It exports `startDevRelayHost` and `bootstrapDevRelayHost`, which connect the relay socket to `window.electronAPI` and tear the host bridge down when the socket closes.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/moderation-br.summary: Applies selected moderation development fixtures to the dev moderator override store and re-exports the fixture contract APIs. Used to simulate moderator roles and scopes, including hidden and reconnect scenarios, while testing moderation browser flows.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/protocol.ts.summary: Defines the JSON message protocol for the dev relay, including call/subscribe/result/event/unsubscribe message shapes. It exports `encodeRelayMessage`, `decodeRelayMessage`, and `serializeRelayError`, making this the place to look for relay wire format and error normalization.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/relay-host.ts.summary: Implements the host-side RPC bridge that receives relay messages and invokes methods on the Electron API object. It resolves dotted method paths defensively, supports one-way subscriptions with cleanup, and serializes failures back to the browser client, so this file is the core of the relay host dispatch logic.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/relay-rpc-cli.summary: Implements the browser-side RPC client for the dev relay, translating method calls and subscriptions into WebSocket messages. It exports `createRelayRpcClient`, tracks pending calls by ID, converts relay errors back into `Error` objects, and feeds subscription events to listeners.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/user-profile-.summary: Returns development-only failure fixtures for user profile reads when `userProfileFixture=unavailable` is present in the URL. It exports `getUserProfileFixture`, which matches `userProfiles.*` paths and forces typed failure states for profile identity lookups and other profile fields.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/websocket.ts.summary: WebSocket connection helpers for the development relay at /__streamfusion-dev. Exports relay roles, socket creation, and retry-based connection waiting with configurable attempts, delay, and testable sleep behavior.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/browse-sn.summary: Bootstraps React Query browse data from persisted desktop snapshots and local LRUs to make streams, categories, search results, followed streams, chat history, and images available immediately on app startup. Validates snapshot freshness and identity, hydrates only missing queries, sanitizes persisted data, and prewarms viewport images before network refreshes.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/cache-inv.summary: Tests the cache invalidation surface for follow mutations, account removal, and platform recovery, verifying the exact React Query keys that are invalidated or removed. It protects the split between follow/channel caches, followed stream caches, and recovery refresh behavior while also checking cache-performance telemetry labels.

Centralizes TanStack Query cache updates after follow mutations, account removal, and platform recovery. Exports helpers to invalidate, remove, and authoritatively filter followed channels, streams, and content while preserving platform-specific cache behavior.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/cache-per.summary: Covers cache-performance telemetry for query surfaces, asserting the 50ms budget rules, p95 aggregation, invalidation dispatch timing, and hook-driven paint/refresh instrumentation. The tests document how `useQueryCachePerformance` distinguishes cache-hit paint from route refresh start and ensure performance samples are recorded against the correct surface labels.

Measures React Query cache-hit paint, route refresh, and invalidation timings against a 50ms budget. Exports the performance hook, sample recording utilities, summaries, reset functions, and a window debug API for investigating query responsiveness.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/cache-pol.summary: Vitest coverage for application data cache tiers, checking stale times, garbage-collection times, polling behavior, local persistence, and TanStack Query option conversion. Guards against collapsing remote and local query caching into a single policy.

Centralized cache policy definitions for remote browsing queries and persisted local user state, including stale times, garbage collection, polling, storage mode, and placeholder behavior. Exports APP_DATA_CACHE_POLICIES, its policy-name type, and getQueryCacheOptions for converting policies into TanStack Query options.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/persisted.summary: Persistent LRU cache for channel metadata backed by `window.electronAPI.store`, keyed by platform and normalized username. Exports hydration, lookup, save, reset, and React subscription hooks for reusing validated Twitch/Kick channel snapshots while enforcing entry count, size, and age limits.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useCatego.summary: Fetches and combines category clips or videos from Twitch and Kick through Electron IPC, normalizing platform-specific response shapes into shared CategoryMediaItem records. Exports media type definitions and useCategoryMedia, which handles platform scope, sorting, filtering, deduplication, loading states, and search-oriented cache policy.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useChanne.summary: Defines React Query keys and hooks for followed channels and channel lookup by username/platform through the Electron API. Results are deduplicated, cache performance is measured, and channel data repairs follow metadata in the follow store.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useFollow.summary: Query helpers for assembling followed videos and clips across a user’s channels, with normalization of heterogeneous backend payloads into a single feed item model. It limits fan-out, filters invalid past videos, deduplicates by platform and id, and supports recent/views sorting plus clip time ranges.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useHistor.summary: Local history query and mutation helpers backed by the history store, exposing a React Query view of in-app playback/history state. It keeps the query cache in sync when items are added, removed, or cleared and measures cache invalidation dispatches for performance tracking.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useInfini.summary: React Query infinite-pagination hooks for top, category, and followed live streams. Calls Electron stream APIs with cursors, platform/category filters, cache policies, query keys, and cache-performance tracking; category queries also support name-based fallback and dataset-specific keys.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useSearch.summary: React Query hooks and helpers for cross-platform search of channels, categories, streams, videos, and clips. Defines stable search keys, normalized queries, progressive paginated fetching, stale-result protection, platform status handling, deduplication, cancellation, and persisted search cache integration.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useStream.summary: React Query hooks for top, category, followed, and channel-specific live streams. Provides stable stream cache keys, followed-stream cache removal, identity-aware snapshot persistence, platform-specific refetch intervals, stream deduplication, and query performance instrumentation.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-ad-element-ob.summary: MutationObserver-based hook that detects and hides Twitch ad DOM elements as they appear, including overlay and banner selectors. Intended for player-side ad suppression, with cleanup and debug logging of every hidden element and total hidden count.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-app-shutdown..summary: App shutdown hook that subscribes to the main-process `app:before-quit` event and forces fast renderer cleanup. It shuts down chat services, marks `window.__shuttingDown`, and clears batched chat state so expensive teardown work does not outlive the process.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-chat-replay.t.summary: React hook for fetching and caching time-bucketed chat replay windows from the Electron video bridge. Deduplicates in-flight requests, supports locators and retries, cancels unused requests, and exposes replay result, loading/error status, and retry controls.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-download-acti.summary: React actions for enqueueing clip and video downloads through the Electron downloads bridge. Detects duplicate queued jobs, requests confirmation when needed, and reports success, cancellation, and failures through toast notifications.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-live-notifica.summary: Bridges Electron live-notification events into the notification store and toast UI, honoring user notification preferences. Toast and open events navigate directly to the corresponding platform stream route.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-stream-record.summary: React action layer for starting, pausing, resuming, stopping, discarding, recovering, opening, and revealing stream recordings through the Electron bridge. Normalizes bridge failures and surfaces operation-specific success and error toasts for recording workflows.

Context-backed external store for stream recording lifecycle state, including active sessions, completion notices, partial recordings, failures, elapsed duration, and quality changes. Subscribes to Electron state updates, preserves monotonic captured duration, provides periodic recording ticks, and exposes accessible live announcements.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useAfterFirstPain.summary: Small React hook that returns `true` only after the first browser paint, using `requestAnimationFrame` and a test-mode shortcut. Use it when looking for post-hydration or deferred-render gating in the UI.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useAuth.ts.summary: React hooks for Twitch and Kick authentication, guest state, initialization, follows, preferences, errors, and combined user display information. Wraps auth-store selectors and actions into reusable UI-facing APIs.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useChatRoomState..summary: Reads optimistic chat room state for a given platform and channel from `useRoomStateStore`, falling back to `DEFAULT_ROOM_STATE` when no entry exists. It is the hook to find if you need room-state lookup by `platform + channelId` without null checks, especially for chat moderation or channel settings UI.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useChatSettingsSy.summary: Test-only helper module exposing inspection and reset utilities for `useChatSettingsSync` internals like the in-flight guard and provenance map. Use this file when searching for hook test helpers, module-scoped state reset, or debug access that must not ship in production bundles.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/persisted.summary: Persistence layer for React Query infinite search results, keyed by normalized query, platform, limit, and live-only state. Hydrates from Electron store, validates and sanitizes saved UnifiedCategory/UnifiedChannel/UnifiedClip/UnifiedVideo pages, and exposes save/get/use hooks so search screens can restore cached results across sessions.

Loads, validates, saves, and deletes versioned query snapshots in the Electron store, preventing stale or mismatched data from being restored. The React hook exposes identity-safe snapshots and prewarms referenced viewport images for faster UI recovery.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/recent-st.summary: Caches a small LRU-like index of recently viewed stream image URLs per platform and channel, then prewarms those images on later visits. Exports rememberRecentStreamImages, prewarmRecentStreamImages, and useRecentStreamImagePrewarm, which together reduce blank thumbnails and improve perceived speed in stream browsing flows.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useCatego.summary: Provides React Query category discovery and aggregation across Twitch and Kick, including progressive previews, viewer-count enrichment from top streams, normalized cross-platform merging, persistence, and cache-performance tracking. Exports category query keys and category hooks used by browse and discovery surfaces.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useChatSettingsSy.summary: Synchronizes Twitch and Kick room moderation settings from initial fetches, WebSocket roomState events, and optimistic store updates with last-write-wins behavior. Exports the useChatSettingsSync lifecycle hook, chatSettingsToPatch translator, and internal test instrumentation for race protection, reconnect refetching, and stale-event handling.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useDebounce.ts.summary: Minimal debounce hook that delays propagating a changing value until a timeout expires. Commonly used for search inputs, filters, and other high-frequency UI state that should not trigger immediate downstream work.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useElectron.ts.summary: React hook collection for talking to Electron's preload bridge, including app version, prerelease metadata, window controls, external links, notifications, and persisted store access. It centralizes renderer-to-main process integration through `window.electronAPI` for desktop-specific behavior.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useHelixPoll.ts.summary: Visibility-aware polling hook for Helix-style endpoints that fetches immediately, then refreshes on an interval only while enabled and the document is visible. It exports `useHelixPoll` plus typed options/result shapes for building polling flows with loading/error state and manual refresh.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useInterval.ts.summary: Declarative interval hook that repeatedly invokes the latest callback without recreating the timer on every render. Used as the reusable timer primitive for polling and other recurring React side effects that need pause/resume semantics.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useIsKickMod.ts.summary: Permission-check hook that determines whether the current authenticated Kick user can moderate a channel, with broadcaster self-moderation, cached moderated-channel lookup, and dev override support. This is the Kick-side gate for showing mod UI without triggering any network hydrate.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useIsTwitchMod.ts.summary: Determines whether the signed-in Twitch user can moderate a channel by checking broadcaster identity or cached moderated-channel IDs. Exports real authority detection plus a development-only mod-role override for forcing moderator UI in chat simulations.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useManagedTimeout.summary: Managed one-shot timeout hook that exposes imperative `start` and `clear` controls while keeping the latest callback and cleaning up on unmount. Useful for auto-hide, re-arming delays, and other resettable timeout workflows in interactive desktop UI.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useSearchHistory..summary: React hook for per-scope search history persistence in `localStorage`, with migration support for legacy flat arrays and capped, de-duplicated recent terms. Exposes `useSearchHistory` plus `SEARCH_HISTORY_SCOPES` for channels, categories, and streams search UIs that need scoped autocomplete or recent-query dropdowns.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useStickyDismisse.summary: React hook that implements a sticky-dismiss suppression gate for live prediction banners, preventing the same prediction ID from reopening after the user closes it. Exports `useStickyDismissedPrediction` for chat/player widgets that need to ignore repeated status updates until a new prediction arrives.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useStreamPlayback.summary: React hook and shared utilities for fetching, caching, prefetching, reloading, and coordinating HLS/DASH/MP4 stream playback URLs across main and mini-player subscribers. Includes platform-aware cache keys, request deduplication, staggered multistream initialization, retry limits, eviction deferral, failure backoff, network status, and playback logging.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useTimeout.ts.summary: Minimal declarative timer hook that runs the latest callback once after a delay and cleans up on delay changes or unmount. Useful anywhere the codebase needs a one-shot timeout without managing `setTimeout` and refs manually.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useUpdater.ts.summary: Updater state hook that bridges the renderer to the Electron updater backend, wiring initial status, progress, and status-change subscriptions into app state. Exposes actions for checking, downloading, installing, and toggling prerelease or auto-check settings, making it the main updater facade for settings and update dialogs.

apps/desktop/src/lib/api-client.ts.summary: Creates the shared Ky-based HTTP client with a 30-second timeout, retry handling for transient network and HTTP failures, and centralized error logging. Exports convenience methods for common HTTP verbs plus the raw Ky instance for callers needing advanced configuration.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useModerationAuth.summary: Resolves whether the current Twitch or Kick user is a broadcaster, moderator, viewer, guest, or unverifiable for a channel. Exports useModerationAuthority plus authority state types and freshness constants; combines authenticated identity, moderated-channel snapshots, scope checks, reconnect handling, expiration, and development fixtures for moderation UI authorization.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useModLog.ts.summary: React Query hook for reading channel moderation history through the Electron mod-log IPC bridge. Exports useModLog, UseModLogOptions, and ModLogEntry, supporting filters, loading/error states, retry, and refresh-counter read-after-write behavior for moderation surfaces.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useNetworkStatus..summary: Provides a reactive React hook over the shared network status store, exposing online state and an immediate connectivity check. Also exports a debug override setter used to simulate offline or online conditions in development and tests.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/usePlatformHealth.summary: Renderer hook that hydrates platform health from `electronAPI.platformHealth`, subscribes to live status changes, and computes an `anyDegraded` aggregate flag. Used by app surfaces that need Twitch/Kick service health, recovery cache invalidation, and status-page details.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useRequireModScop.summary: Checks whether the signed-in Twitch token contains moderation OAuth scopes and identifies missing channel-moderation EventSub scope groups. Exports useRequireModScopes and reconnect option/result types, enabling mod-action surfaces to prompt lazy re-consent and retry actions after authorization.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/useResolveTwitchC.summary: Resolves a Twitch channel login into its numeric broadcaster ID and display metadata through the Helix-backed Electron API. Exports useResolveTwitchChannel and ResolvedTwitchChannel, with React Query caching, no automatic retries, loading/null results, and a development ID override for moderation routes.

apps/desktop/src/lib/stream-route-preloa.summary: Preload and startup-warmup helper for the Stream route and its nested chat module in the desktop app. Exports `preloadStreamExperience()` for intent-based route prefetching and `scheduleStreamExperienceStartupPrewarm()` for a one-shot post-first-paint `requestAnimationFrame` warmup with status markers on `window.__streamExperiencePrewarm`.

apps/desktop/src/lib/utils.ts.summary: Shared frontend utility functions for Tailwind class merging, viewer counts, relative times, durations, languages, uptime, and cross-platform category normalization. Exports formatting helpers plus category equivalence and winner-selection logic used across discovery and following views.

apps/desktop/src/lib/viewport-image-prew.summary: Viewport image prewarming queue that resolves proxied image URLs, loads them with bounded concurrency, and retains recently warmed `HTMLImageElement`s to keep image-heavy feeds responsive. Exports `prewarmViewportImages()` plus test helpers to reset state and inspect retained URLs, with constants controlling queue size, concurrency, and retention.

apps/desktop/src/main.ts.summary: Electron main-process entry point for StreamFusion, coordinating application startup, user-data paths, IPC registration, authentication, windows, custom media protocols, logging, diagnostics, services, crash recovery, and shutdown behavior. Also configures development and production remote debugging, optional Chromium net logging, and early process-level instrumentation.

apps/desktop/src/lib/cross-logger.ts.summary: Cross-process logging adapter for code shared between Electron main and renderer without pulling `electron-log` into the renderer bundle. Exports a `logger` with `debug/info/warn/error` plus `setMainLogSink` so calls can route to the main logger, the renderer IPC bridge, or console fallback during boot and tests.

apps/desktop/src/lib/dev-browser-media-u.summary: URL rewrite helpers for the dev browser media proxy used in local playback and media inspection. Exports `DEV_BROWSER_MEDIA_PATH`, `buildDevBrowserMediaUrl`, and rewrite helpers that convert Twitch clip/media URLs and nested playback values into proxied dev-server URLs.

apps/desktop/src/lib/duration.ts.summary: Flexible duration parser that accepts seconds, colon-delimited time strings, and `h/m/s` unit syntax. Exports `parseDurationSeconds` for turning user-entered duration strings into positive second counts, returning `null` for invalid input.

apps/desktop/src/lib/error-toast.ts.summary: Standardized error toast helper built on `sonner` with copy-to-clipboard support. Exports `showErrorToast`, which shows a longer-lived error notification and adds a "Copy error" action for faster bug reporting.

apps/desktop/src/lib/id-utils.ts.summary: Centralizes platform-aware channel and stream identifiers so Twitch and Kick records cannot collide in React keys, Maps, Sets, or follow lookups. Exports key builders, identity matching, duplicate channel/stream merging, metadata selection, and case-insensitive username fallback logic for inconsistent platform IDs.

apps/desktop/src/lib/languages.ts.summary: Static broadcaster language list and display-name resolver for Twitch/Kick filter UIs. Exports `BROADCAST_LANGUAGES` and `getLanguageDisplayName`, using `Intl.DisplayNames` to turn ISO 639-1 codes into human-readable labels.

apps/desktop/src/lib/live-notification-i.summary: Helpers for normalizing live-notification usernames and choosing a stable display name from multiple candidates. Exports `normalizeLiveNotificationUsername` and `resolveLiveNotificationDisplayName`, which match names case-insensitively and prefer a non-raw display label when available.

apps/desktop/src/lib/live-notification-p.summary: Per-channel live alert preference logic that merges defaults, checks platform toggles, and determines whether a channel should receive notifications. Exports helpers for channel keys, preference normalization, eligibility checks, per-channel updates, and platform-field mapping.

apps/desktop/src/lib/managed-interval.ts.summary: Backend-safe wrapper around `setInterval` that returns an idempotent stop handle and optionally unrefs the timer. Exports `createManagedInterval`, used as the sanctioned recurring timer abstraction for Electron main/Node code.

apps/desktop/src/lib/proxied-image-url.t.summary: Image URL allowlist and proxy resolver for Twitch/Kick avatars, previews, and other remote images. Exports `isAllowedPlatformImageUrl`, `resolveProxiedImageSrc`, `resolveProxiedSrc`, and related scheme constants so the app can safely rewrite supported platform images through a proxy or dev browser media endpoint.

apps/desktop/src/lib/settings-toast.ts.summary: Single stable success toast for settings auto-save flows. Exports `notifySettingsSaved`, which deduplicates rapid updates by reusing a fixed toast ID so sliders and other live settings do not spam the user.

apps/desktop/src/lib/sleep.ts.summary: Defines promise-based delay utilities for imperative async timing such as retry backoff, including a physically cancellable timer with optional Node/Electron unref support. Callers can distinguish normal completion from explicit cancellation without faking observable event waits.
