apps/desktop/src/lib/stream-recording-pr.summary: Presentation-layer labels and duration formatting for stream recording status UI. Exports phase/lifecycle label maps and `formatCapturedDuration` to turn recording state and elapsed seconds into human-readable text.

apps/desktop/src/pages/AGENTS.md.summary: Directory-level guide for route page components in the desktop app. Documents the TanStack Router page structure, page responsibilities, store/IPC boundaries, and anti-patterns to search when wiring route-level UI like Home, SearchResults, Stream, Video, and Settings.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Categories/index..summary: Categories browsing page that fetches cached Twitch and Kick categories, filters them by search text, and renders results through a virtualized category grid. Handles loading, first-paint gating, empty states, and category count messaging.

apps/desktop/src/pages/CategoryDetail/co.summary: Renders category-scoped Twitch and Kick clips or videos in responsive card grids using the useCategoryMedia query hook. Handles loading skeletons, platform-specific failures and retries, empty states, media normalization, and clip playback dialogs with refetch-on-error behavior.

apps/desktop/src/pages/CategoryDetail/in.summary: Category detail page for browsing live streams, clips, and videos within a Twitch or Kick category. Manages route-search canonicalization, platform/category matching, language/tag/sort filters, infinite stream loading, cross-platform category identity, and tabbed media content.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Downloads/index.t.summary: Downloads page for monitoring and managing queued video and clip download jobs through the Electron downloads API. Renders status, progress, thumbnails, cancellation, file actions, removal, error recovery, queue-change subscriptions, and thumbnail prewarming.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Following/index.t.summary: Following dashboard for live streams, videos, clips, categories, and channels across Twitch and Kick. Combines local and remote follows, deduplicates platform identities, supports filtering, debounced search, sorting, pagination/load-more behavior, thumbnail preloading, refresh/error states, and clip playback dialogs.

apps/desktop/src/pages/History/index.tsx.summary: Watch history page for listing, navigating to, validating, and removing previously watched streams, videos, and clips. Integrates history queries and actions with route navigation, playback URL verification, clip metadata recovery, ClipDialog playback, and clear-history controls.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Home/components/l.summary: Home-page section component that renders the "Live Channels" block using `StreamGrid`, taking a `streams` list plus loading state and showing an 8-item skeleton grid while data is fetching. Search for this file when working on the featured/home browse layout or the stream-card grid that surfaces live content.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Home/index.tsx.summary: Top-level `HomePage` route for the desktop app, wiring `useTopStreams` into a featured-stream hero, a live-now section, and a browse-categories CTA. Handles the empty/error state for stream loading and defers rendering until after first paint to reduce layout jank on initial load.

apps/desktop/src/pages/index.ts.summary: Central page-routing module that exports lazy-loaded React page components, including moderation, streaming, settings, history, and download pages. Provides preloadable route creation plus staged requestAnimationFrame-based chunk preloading to reduce initial bundle cost and warm commonly used page modules.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Mod/AGENTS.md.summary: Documentation for the moderation admin surface under `/mod`, describing the page layout, platform coverage, invariants, and anti-patterns for Twitch and Kick moderation flows. Use this as the map for moderation routing, retention settings, mod-log access, and the channel-level component tree.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Mod/channel/Chann.summary: Twitch channel banned-user management component that fetches banned users through the Electron Twitch API, displays expiration and moderation metadata, and supports optimistic per-row unbanning with toast errors. Provides a Kick-specific informational state because Kick lacks a public banned-user list endpoint.

Broadcaster-facing Twitch channel engagement panel for active predictions and polls. Fetches both Helix resources on mount, refresh triggers, and a 30-second interval, then renders active statuses, outcomes, votes, loading, and empty states.

Broadcaster-only Twitch moderator roster with username resolution, add/remove mutations, loading and error states, and per-row removal feedback. Synchronizes the moderated-channels store when the signed-in user is added or removed from the channel.

Standalone mod-log feed for a channel, mirroring the in-chat moderation history tab but without the user popout dependency. Exports `ChannelModLogFeed` and provides action/username filters, incremental paging, timestamp formatting, and verified/error/partial states via `useModLog`.

Moderation UI for listing and resolving Twitch channel unban requests. Filters by request status, loads through the Electron Twitch API, and supports approve/deny actions with optional resolution text and toast feedback.

Broadcaster-only Twitch VIP roster with add and remove controls. Resolves usernames to Twitch users, calls VIP mutation operations through the Electron API, updates local table state, and reports failures or successes with toasts.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Mod/channel/ModCh.summary: Route wrapper for `/mod/kick/$channel` that reads the channel slug from TanStack Router and passes it into the shared mod-channel page. This keeps Kick and Twitch channel moderation flows on the same shell while differing only by platform and route param shape.

Shared per-channel moderation dashboard shell for Twitch and Kick, responsible for resolving the channel identity, checking moderation authority, and rendering the channel-scoped sections. It ties together retention controls, mod-log history, banned users, VIPs, moderators, unban requests, and engagement tools under one route-driven page.

Route wrapper for `/mod/twitch/$channel` that extracts the Twitch broadcaster login from the URL and forwards it to the shared mod-channel page. It exists to keep platform-specific routing thin while the core moderation UI stays centralized.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Mod/channel/Reten.summary: Reusable retention settings card for a single moderation-log scope, with a days input and Forever toggle persisted through `window.electronAPI.retention`. It is used by the per-channel moderation pages and other retention UIs to edit channel-scoped or global log-retention rules.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Mod/ChannelList.t.summary: Moderation index component that gathers Twitch channels the user moderates plus their own channel, and the signed-in Kick channel. Renders platform-specific links and badges for navigating to per-channel moderation pages, including loading and empty states.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Mod/GlobalRetenti.summary: Wrapper around the shared retention card for the global mod-log retention default shown on the /mod index. Use this file when searching for the global-vs-channel retention UI or the default retention scope that per-channel pages override.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Mod/index.tsx.summary: Top-level moderation landing page that combines the moderated channel list with global retention settings. Provides a refresh action that rehydrates the moderated-channels store so newly granted Twitch moderation access appears without a full reload.

apps/desktop/src/pages/MultiStream/index.summary: MultiStream workspace page that renders multiple streams in grid or focus layouts with an optional chat rail. Connects multistream store state to layout controls, stream slot cleanup, active-channel metadata, Kick badges, and the shared ChatPanel.

apps/desktop/src/pages/preloadable-compo.summary: Utility for creating a React component that can be preloaded externally without forcing a second React.lazy suspense pass. It exports `createPreloadableComponent`, which caches the loaded module, preserves preload errors, and renders immediately when the component has already been fetched.

apps/desktop/src/pages/SearchResults/ind.summary: Unified search results page for channels, live streams, videos, clips, and categories across Twitch and Kick. Handles tab and platform filtering, live-only filtering, ranked/infinite channel pagination, verified badges, clip playback selection, and related-content dialogs.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Settings/index.ts.summary: Comprehensive application settings page with tabbed navigation for playback, notifications, player controls, buffering, multiview, chat, ad blocking, proxy, predictions, integrations, API tokens, updates, logs, bug reports, and app information. Centralizes settings metadata and control definitions while connecting preference stores, authentication, updater flows, notification preferences, and development-only diagnostics panels.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Stream/index.tsx.summary: Main Twitch/Kick stream viewing page that resolves route channel data, playback URLs, live/offline state, chat, related content, recording controls, theater mode, and persistent player behavior. Exports StreamPage and preloadChatPanel for stream routing and lazy chat loading.

apps/desktop/src/pages/Video/index.tsx.summary: React route page for viewing Twitch and Kick VODs or clips. Resolves playback URLs and metadata, handles subscriber-only and retry/error states, records history, and renders channel details, sharing, downloading, follow actions, and related content.

apps/desktop/src/preload/AGENTS.md.summary: Developer guide for the Electron preload context bridge, documenting the security boundary between sandboxed renderer code and privileged main-process IPC. Defines electronAPI conventions, IPC channel contracts, listener cleanup, sensitive-token restrictions, namespace coverage, extension steps, anti-patterns, and related shared/backend files.

apps/desktop/src/preload/index.ts.summary: Electron preload bridge exposing a typed, security-scoped renderer API through contextBridge and IPC. Groups app lifecycle, window controls, theme, storage, OAuth/authentication, platform data, streaming, moderation, downloads, captions, and other main-process capabilities used by the renderer.

apps/desktop/src/preload/one-shot-ipc.ts.summary: Utility that turns an initial preload snapshot into a one-time cached response and then falls back to live IPC requests on later calls. It solves cold-start hydration for one read only, which is useful when a startup value should not be reused after mutations or refreshes.

apps/desktop/src/preload/slot.ts.summary: Dedicated preload bridge for StreamSlot WebContentsView renderers, exposing only slot-specific load/mute/quality/buffer/unload listeners plus crash, metrics, and playback reporting back to main. It enforces a narrow security boundary for the embedded player and is the place to look for slot lifecycle IPC and main-to-slot dispatch.

apps/desktop/src/providers/query-provide.summary: Configures the shared TanStack QueryClient for caching, retries, refetching, mutation safety, and confirmed network connectivity. Provides QueryProvider, connectivity synchronization, browse snapshot bootstrapping, and draggable development-only React Query Devtools.

apps/desktop/src/renderer/follow-hydrati.summary: Pre-React hydration bootstrap for follow state. Exports `FOLLOW_HYDRATION_INVOKED_MARK` and `hydrateFollowsBeforeRendererMount`, which marks performance timing and hydrates the follow store before the renderer mounts to avoid snapshot mismatches.

apps/desktop/src/renderer/logging/consol.summary: Console patching layer for the renderer process. Exports `installConsoleIntercept`, which hijacks `console.log/info/warn/error/debug` and forwards them to the IPC-backed renderer logger while preserving the original methods for uninstall and fallback behavior.

apps/desktop/src/renderer/logging/logger.summary: Renderer-side logging facade that forwards structured log payloads to the main process. Exports `logger` and `LogLevel`, using `window.electronAPI.logs.write` when available and falling back to `console` for early boot, teardown, or test contexts.

apps/desktop/src/renderer/logging/networ.summary: Online/offline monitor for the renderer. Exports `installNetworkMonitor`, which attaches `window.online` and `window.offline` listeners, logs the initial connectivity state, and emits transitions through the renderer logger.

apps/desktop/src/renderer/logging/render.summary: Global crash hooks for renderer uncaught errors and promise rejections. Exports `installRendererErrorHooks`, wiring `window.error` and `window.unhandledrejection` into structured logger output so browser-only failures land in the session log with stack, filename, and location metadata.

apps/desktop/src/renderer.tsx.summary: Electron renderer entrypoint that initializes app-wide instrumentation before React renders. Installs console interception, error hooks, and network monitoring, conditionally loads dev-only moderation and browser-relay fixtures, then mounts `App` into `#root` with `createRoot`.

apps/desktop/src/routes/category-detail-.summary: Search-parameter validator for category detail routing. Exports `CategoryDetailSearch` and `validateCategoryDetailSearch`, normalizing tab/platform/language/sort filters and coercing `otherId` into a stable string for URL-driven category views.

apps/desktop/src/routes/router.tsx.summary: Defines the TanStack React Router route tree for browsing, following, categories, search, streams, videos, settings, multistream, history, downloads, and moderation pages. Adds typed search-parameter validation, hash history, lazy-page Suspense loading, and shared AppLayout nesting.

apps/desktop/src/search/category-search-.summary: Search-ranking and deduplication logic for category results, including token-based fuzzy matching, edit-distance scoring, and exact-name cross-platform merging. It is the contract layer that decides which `UnifiedCategory` entries survive search, how they are ordered, and when Twitch/Kick duplicates collapse into one cross-platform result.

apps/desktop/src/search/search-normaliza.summary: Provides shared Unicode-aware search normalization for tokenizing queries, removing accents, lowercasing, preserving emoji graphemes, and compacting identities. Used by channel search matching and ranking to make comparisons consistent.

apps/desktop/src/search/search-result-va.summary: Runtime validation and normalization for unified search results across channels, streams, categories, videos, and clips, with type guards that reject malformed backend payloads. It also provides `sanitizeSearchResultCollection`, which filters invalid items and counts rejects so the rest of the search UI can work with trusted `Unified*` data.

apps/desktop/src/shared/adblock-types.ts.summary: Defines the shared type and configuration contract for Twitch VAFT-inspired ad blocking, including stream state, playlist resolutions, player fallbacks, ad detection, buffering fixes, access tokens, and auto-updatable patterns. Exports default ad-block settings, detection patterns, status types, and createStreamInfo for initializing runtime state.

apps/desktop/src/shared/AGENTS.md.summary: Documents the shared IPC contract layer between Electron main and renderer processes, including file responsibilities, channel naming, payload typing, security invariants, and procedures for adding shared contracts. Use it to find the canonical locations for IPC channels, auth/chat/ad-block types, preload wiring, and process-boundary rules.

apps/desktop/src/shared/auth-types.ts.summary: Shared authentication contracts for Twitch and Kick across desktop main/renderer IPC. Defines OAuth tokens, encrypted token storage, canonical platform scopes, user profiles, follows, account-follow write queues/results, and live notification payloads used by auth, sync, moderation, and notification services.

apps/desktop/src/shared/browser-event-em.summary: Browser-safe `EventEmitter` polyfill that mirrors the Node event API for code bundled into the renderer where `node:events` is unavailable. Exports `BrowserEventEmitter` as `EventEmitter` so shared chat and IPC-adjacent code can use a consistent event abstraction in both browser and Electron contexts.

apps/desktop/src/shared/category-media-t.summary: Request and response contracts for category-scoped clips and videos from Twitch or Kick. Covers pagination, date/view sorting, time ranges, filtering, media metadata, availability, and upstream error states used by category browsing surfaces.

apps/desktop/src/shared/chat-replay-type.summary: Shared contracts for loading and cancelling time-windowed chat replay alongside video playback. Defines replay senders, badges, text/emote fragments, platform video locators, playback snapshots, pagination, capability states, and IPC success/error wrappers.

apps/desktop/src/shared/chat-types.ts.summary: Core cross-platform Twitch/Kick chat model used by live chat rendering, moderation history, and cosmetic enrichment. Defines badges, emotes, 7TV/BTTV/FFZ cosmetics, parsed content fragments, message and notice variants, known users, deletion/ban metadata, highlights, replies, and presentation state.

apps/desktop/src/shared/download-types.t.summary: Shared download queue contracts for clips and videos across desktop processes. Models download requests and sources, lifecycle statuses, byte/progress reporting, retry metadata, output formats, partial files, and queue snapshots consumed by download services and UI.

apps/desktop/src/shared/electron.d.ts.summary: Global TypeScript declaration that adds the preload-exposed `electronAPI` object onto `window`. This is the bridge typing file to find the renderer-side Electron API surface without searching the preload implementation itself.

apps/desktop/src/shared/ipc-channels.ts.summary: Central registry of type-safe IPC channel names and request-related imports shared by Electron main, preload, and renderer processes. Defines constants for lifecycle, window management, authentication, follows, preferences, proxying, notifications, discovery, channels, streams, search, and other cross-process operations.

apps/desktop/src/shared/local-caption-ty.summary: Shared TypeScript contracts for local speech-caption model installation, recognizer sessions, PCM audio chunks, word-timed caption results, and model/audio action responses. Used by caption download state, streaming recognition, sequencing, and renderer-to-main IPC.

apps/desktop/src/shared/mod-log-types.ts.summary: Shared moderation log schema for renderer/main IPC, defining mod-log entry shapes, query filters, retention scopes, and insert/coverage result unions. Useful when searching for Twitch/Kick moderation history, provenance tracking, or IPC-safe replacements for database-service types.

apps/desktop/src/shared/search-types.ts.summary: Shared search request/response contracts for cross-platform content search, including channels, streams, categories, videos, and clips. Defines session-scoped result envelopes, pagination cursors, retry/error states, and the platform error model used by search workers and the UI.

apps/desktop/src/shared/sherpa-onnx-node.summary: Type declarations for the `sherpa-onnx-node` speech-recognition package, exposing the online recognizer and stream APIs used for streaming ASR integration. This file exists to make the Node module importable from TypeScript without bundling implementation code.

apps/desktop/src/shared/slot-presence-co.summary: Pure resolver that maps slot presence plus the user’s background-quality preference into the concrete playback config for a stream slot. Centralizes the renderer-OOM PRD slot matrix, including focused/background/hidden behavior, buffer sizing, quality mode, and mute state.

apps/desktop/src/shared/slot-types.ts.summary: Shared slot lifecycle and IPC event types for stream slot management across main and renderer processes. Defines presence states, quality/buffer configs, load/unload events, and the retry affordance used by the crash-recovery overlay.

apps/desktop/src/shared/stream-recording.summary: Defines the domain model for livestream recording requests, active sessions, quality changes, gaps, output artifacts, recovery journals, lifecycle snapshots, notices, and start/recovery action results. Used across recording orchestration, persistence/recovery, UI state, and completion or failure notifications.

apps/desktop/src/shared/svg.d.ts.summary: Module declarations that let TypeScript import SVG assets either as URLs or as React components via `?react`. This supports the Vite SVG pipeline and keeps icon/component imports type-safe in the renderer.

apps/desktop/src/shared/timeout-moderati.summary: Shared timeout moderation contracts for creating a timeout binding, validating snapshot policy, and submitting timeout actions. Captures the policy limits, actor roles, revalidation paths, and structured failure codes used by moderator workflows.

apps/desktop/src/shared/twitch-playlist-.summary: Minimal result union for fetching a Twitch playlist, separating successful HTTP text retrieval from typed request/network failures. Useful for code that needs to branch on playlist fetch success without throwing exceptions.

apps/desktop/src/shared/user-profile-typ.summary: Shared identity and profile-field state types for resolving public Twitch/Kick user data, channels, follows, and account-created metadata. Models known/negative/unavailable/reconnect-required states so profile fetchers and UI can represent partial identity data consistently.

apps/desktop/src/slot-renderer/index.htm.summary: Standalone HTML shell for the StreamFusion slot WebContentsView, intentionally rendering only a full-bleed `<video>` element. This is the per-stream crash-isolated renderer entrypoint that loads `main.ts` and relies on the preload bridge for IPC.

apps/desktop/src/store/chat-store.ts.summary: Performance-focused Zustand store for per-channel chat messages and known users. Provides canonical platform/channel keys, message batching, ID-based deduplication with emote-rich replacement, configurable message limits, trim hysteresis, and memory-conscious user metadata merging for high-volume chats.

apps/desktop/src/store/dev-mod-override-.summary: Zustand dev-only override store for forcing Twitch moderator and broadcaster conditions so mod-only UI flows can be tested without real permissions. It exports `useDevModOverrideStore` with flags and setters for mod role, scopes, whisper visibility, resolved broadcaster id, and broadcaster identity, and plugs into debug/testing surfaces.

apps/desktop/src/store/emote-store.ts.summary: Persistent Zustand store for loading, caching, searching, and organizing Twitch/Kick emotes from first-party and third-party providers such as 7TV, BTTV, and FFZ. Tracks per-platform and per-channel loading, viewer-scoped recent emotes, favorites, provider preferences, cache invalidation, and emote lookup maps.

apps/desktop/src/store/follow-store.ts.summary: Persistent Zustand store for local and account-backed channel follows across Twitch and Kick. Provides follow/unfollow mutations, source tracking, pending account-action reconciliation, hydration, metadata repair, per-channel concurrency guards, authoritative cache updates, and account-write event handling.

apps/desktop/src/store/history-store.ts.summary: Persistent Zustand store for recently viewed videos, clips, and streams from Twitch or Kick. Adds or bumps items by unique ID, limits history to 200 entries, and supports clearing or removing individual playback-history records.

apps/desktop/src/store/moderated-channel.summary: Zustand store for tracking Twitch broadcaster IDs and Kick channel slugs where the signed-in user has moderator authority. Hydrates Twitch moderation data through Electron/Helix, applies live Twitch IRC and Kick badge updates, records authority results, refreshes stale cache entries, and clears platform data on logout.

apps/desktop/src/slot-renderer/main.ts.summary: Vanilla TypeScript entrypoint for the Slot WebContentsView renderer that boots HLS.js playback in each StreamSlot, handles mute/unload lifecycle, and reports playback events back through `window.slotAPI`. It exists as the minimal renderer-OOM slice, separate from the main React app and host chrome, and is the place to search for `onLoadStream`, `onSetMute`, HLS attach/detach, and WebContentsView player teardown.

apps/desktop/src/store/adblock-store.ts.summary: Small persisted Zustand store for Twitch ad-blocking preferences, exposing `useAdBlockStore` with enable/disable and toggle actions. Search this file when you need the localStorage-backed ad-block flag or the default-on Twitch stream ad-block setting.

apps/desktop/src/store/AGENTS.md.summary: Directory guide for the desktop `store/` layer, documenting the Zustand store conventions, backend-sync patterns, persistence rules, and where to look for auth, follows, volume, multistream, and UI state. Useful as the index for locating store responsibilities, selectors, and IPC-backed state flows before editing any `*-store.ts` file.

apps/desktop/src/store/app-store.ts.summary: Application-wide Zustand store for UI state such as sidebar collapse/open behavior, theater mode, home carousel timing, active multistream slots, and the debug overlay. Exports `useAppStore` plus `clampHomeCarouselIntervalMs` and the carousel interval constants, making this the file to search for persisted UI preferences and multi-stream layout state.

apps/desktop/src/store/auth-store.ts.summary: Zustand authentication store coordinating Twitch, Kick, guest mode, local follows, and user preferences in the desktop renderer. Initializes and refreshes provider sessions through Electron IPC, exposes login/logout and follow-sync actions, tracks reconnect and error states, and invalidates related query caches after mutations.

apps/desktop/src/store/multistream-store.summary: Persisted Zustand store for multistream playback configuration, including stream slots, favorites, grid/focus layout, chat selection, mute and volume controls, stream ordering, capacity limits, and background video quality. Exports migration and validation helpers that preserve preferences across schema versions and normalize corrupt persisted values.

apps/desktop/src/store/notification-stor.summary: Persisted Zustand store for live in-app notifications, with deduping, unread tracking via `readAt`, bulk-mark-read, dismiss, and clear actions. Exports `useNotificationStore` and the `LiveNotification` / `LiveNotificationInput` types, and is the obvious file to find live notification inbox state and storage limits.

apps/desktop/src/store/persisted-chat-hi.summary: Local chat-history cache layer that hydrates, validates, bounds, and primes persisted Twitch/Kick message history using the Electron store and the main `useChatStore`. Exports hydration and save/prime helpers such as `hydratePersistedChatHistory`, `getPersistedChatHistory`, `primePersistedChatHistoryIntent`, `primePersistedChatHistoryIntentAsync`, and `savePersistedChatHistory`, making it the file to search for LRU-style chat history restoration and cold-start cache priming.

apps/desktop/src/store/pip-store.ts.summary: Zustand store for picture-in-picture mini-player state, tracking the current stream, whether PiP is active, and whether the user is on the stream page. Exports `usePipStore` plus `PipStreamInfo`, and is where to look for route-aware PiP activation and close behavior.

apps/desktop/src/store/playback-position.summary: Persisted Zustand store for resume-playback data keyed by platform and video ID, including saved position, duration, timestamps, and optional metadata for continue-watching UI. Exports `usePlaybackPositionStore` and implements cleanup rules like minimum watch time, completion threshold removal, and max stored items, so it is the file to find playback resume and history-retention logic.

apps/desktop/src/store/reconnect-dialog-.summary: Zustand store for the reconnect/auth-scopes dialog used when a platform connection needs reauthorization. Exports `useReconnectDialogStore` plus the `ReconnectPhase` and `ReconnectDialogPayload` types, with locking logic for submit/revalidate flows and a callback hook for post-reconnect refresh.

apps/desktop/src/store/room-state-store..summary: Per-channel Zustand store for chat moderation room settings keyed by platform and channel ID. Tracks slow mode, followers-only, subscribers-only, emote-only, Twitch unique-chat and shield mode, and Kick account-age settings, with optimistic updates, reset behavior, and a reusable room-state key helper.

apps/desktop/src/store/update-store.ts.summary: Persisted Zustand store for the desktop app auto-update flow, covering status, update metadata, download progress, and user preferences. Exports `useUpdateStore`, `UpdateStatus`, `UpdateInfo`, `UpdateProgress`, and `CheckFrequency`, with backend state hydration and runtime validation for update statuses.

apps/desktop/src/store/user-popout-chat-.summary: Helper selectors for finding a user's recent chat messages in a channel and reconciling a selected message against the live message list. Exports `selectRecentUserMessages`, `selectLatestAuthoredMessage`, and `reconcileSelectedMessage`, used for popout chat context, reply matching, and user-message lookup.

apps/desktop/src/store/volume-store.ts.summary: Global persisted volume and mute store for the desktop player, keeping audio settings stable across stream changes and app restarts. Exports `useVolumeStore` with `setVolume`, `setMuted`, and `toggleMute`, plus clamping logic for 0-100 volume values.

apps/desktop/src/vite-env.d.ts.summary: Vite and SVGR ambient type declarations for the desktop app. Defines typed import-meta environment variables used for Kick client configuration and browser-development flags.

apps/desktop/tailwind.config.mjs.summary: Tailwind configuration for the desktop app theme, including brand/platform color tokens, dark-mode support, typography plugin, font stack, radii, and custom animations. This is the place to find the project's design system primitives and utility class generation rules.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/adblock-loade.summary: Vitest coverage for Twitch HLS ad-block loader helpers, mocking `hls.js` and the ad-block service to verify loader factory behavior and HLS config shape. Includes behavior checks for master playlist, media playlist, and segment URL detection patterns used by the Twitch ad-block pipeline.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/adblock-servi.summary: Vitest coverage for the Twitch adblock service state machine in `twitch-adblock-service`, including init/update config, status queries, playlist processing, auth header setup, and ad-segment detection. Useful when searching for ad-block playlist rewriting, Twitch HLS master/media playlist handling, or the service’s callback and blank-video helpers.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/adblock-store.summary: Minimal store-level test for the Zustand adblock store, pinning the user-facing `enableAdBlock` default and guarding against silent default-state regressions. Useful for finding the app-level adblock flag, Zustand store expectations, and default-enabled behavior.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/adblock-types.summary: Vitest contract tests for the default Twitch ad-block configuration. Locks the VAFT client ID, stitched ad signifier, fallback player types, ad stripping behavior, reload policy, and request timing so configuration drift cannot silently break ad recovery.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/backup-stream.summary: Integration-style tests for the backup stream flow that cycles Twitch `playerType` variants, validates GQL access-token request assumptions, and checks token/domain stripping behavior. Useful when searching for VAFT fallback logic, player-type iteration, usher URL handling, or the config values that drive ad-free stream recovery.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/cosmetic-inje.summary: Vitest unit tests for the Electron cosmetic injection service, covering enable/disable state, idempotent per-window CSS and scriptlet injection, graceful errors, Twitch ad selectors, video visibility shielding, and abort-on-property-read behavior. Useful for finding tests around BrowserWindow webContents injection, adblock cosmetic filters, IPC contracts, and injected CSS/scriptlets.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/hevc-handling.summary: Vitest tests for Twitch playlist rewriting when HEVC streams are detected during ads, focusing on master-playlist parsing and fallback behavior. It exercises codec detection for `hev1`, `hvc1`, `avc1`, and `av01`, making this the place to find HEVC-to-AVC compatibility logic in the adblock pipeline.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/integration.t.summary: End-to-end Vitest coverage for the Twitch ad-blocking pipeline, including stream initialization, master and media playlist processing, preroll and midroll detection, ad segment stripping, clean playback preservation, recovery, status callbacks, and player interruption behavior. Useful for finding integration tests around twitch-adblock-service exports such as processMasterPlaylist, processMediaPlaylist, getAdBlockStatus, and stream lifecycle management.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/playback-adva.summary: Vitest coverage for the playback-advanced preference-to-adblock override resolver and the live Twitch adblock config path. Verifies player-type and HEVC preferences map to the real config fields, default preferences stay a no-op, and device-id randomization clears and regenerates the persisted localStorage value.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/segment-strip.summary: Vitest suite for Twitch HLS ad segment stripping when backup streams are unavailable. Exercises playlist parsing, stitched-ad detection, tracking-URL markers, preroll vs midroll status, and prefetch removal in the adblock service.

apps/desktop/tests/AGENTS.md.summary: Developer guide for the desktop test suite. Documents test directory structure, commands, regression-focused quality standards, Keep/Rewrite/Delete audit verdicts, required Guards comments, failure-state coverage, and performance budgets.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/m3u8-parsing..summary: Vitest coverage for Twitch HLS/M3U8 parsing in the ad-block pipeline, using realistic master and media playlist fixtures to verify quality variants, codec/bandwidth preservation, channel normalization, and ad-marker handling. This file is a regression suite for `twitch-adblock-service` exports like `processMasterPlaylist`, `processMediaPlaylist`, `initAdBlockService`, `clearStreamInfo`, and `getAdBlockStatus`.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/network-adblo.summary: Vitest tests for the network-level URL blocker that decides whether Twitch, Kick, and third-party ad or telemetry requests should be blocked. It exercises the `networkAdBlockService` API (`shouldBlock`, `enable`, `disable`, `toggle`, `isActive`, `getStats`) against ad-server, tracking, and allowlist patterns.

apps/desktop/tests/adblock/parent-domain.summary: Regression tests for the Twitch ad-block flow that strips `parent_domains` from access-token JSON and usher URLs so backup streams are not treated as embedded players. This file validates `twitch-adblock-service` behavior around token parsing, URL parameter cleanup, ad detection, and graceful handling of malformed or missing token fields.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/api/platforms.summary: Vitest coverage for Kick category endpoint behavior. Verifies official public v2 category retrieval, bounded pagination, ID lookup, anonymous search and matching, response mapping, and fallback to private category APIs when the official request fails.

Vitest coverage for Kick channel endpoint behavior, including public channel normalization, official account-status classification, platform-health handling, browser-window serialization, profile/avatar fallback, and safe account-removal decisions. Mocks Electron BrowserWindow, Kick user/video endpoints, and platform health to test degraded networks and ambiguous provider responses.

Vitest suite for Kick chat history retrieval, focused on loading channel message history through an Electron `BrowserWindow`, handling health-state gating, JSON parsing failures, and cleanup in `finally`. This is the test file to find when working on `getKickChannelHistory`, message/pinned-message extraction, URL encoding, and timeout or server-error resilience.

Vitest coverage for `mapKickChatroomToSettings`, the Kick chatroom-to-unified-settings normalizer used by the backend Kick channel endpoints. These tests protect against stale server-side mode values leaking into disabled modes, verify defensive handling of non-boolean flags, and document that `accountAge` is not populated from the initial fetch.

Vitest coverage for Kick clip endpoint adapters, including channel and category discovery, response mapping, duration formatting, pagination, sorting, request headers, timeout signals, missing fields, and transport or HTTP failures. Uses an Electron net.fetch mock to validate URL construction and resilient empty-result behavior.

JSON fixture representing multiple backward-pagination pages for Kick chat replay, including cursors, timestamps, and messages that straddle a requested replay window. Useful when searching for replay pagination, cursor chaining, or boundary-condition test data for chat history backfill.

Single-page Kick chat replay fixture with one message, sender identity, badges, emote markup, and pagination cursor metadata. This supports tests for chat replay parsing and message normalization, especially when looking for Kick message payload shape examples.

Vitest coverage for Kick followed-channel import and authenticated follow-write endpoints, emphasizing Bearer-first fetching and failure classification. Tests validate response mapping, empty-follow handling, missing tokens, auth failures, Cloudflare challenges, parse errors, network errors, warning deduplication, abort behavior, canonical IDs, and retry-safe web-session mutations.

Tests for `GRID_READY_PREDICATE`, the DOM predicate string injected into the Kick follows page to detect when the followed-channels grid is ready. The suite checks the exact readiness heuristic against rendered cards, loading states, and pages without the follow heading.

Vitest contract tests for Kick chat replay ingestion, covering replay-page parsing, playback-relative history URL construction, VOD metadata fallback, malformed-row tolerance, and AbortError/cancellation behavior in the browser fallback path. This file is the best search target for Kick VOD chat replay normalization, cursor pagination, emote/badge mapping, and transport fallback logic.

Tests the Kick CDN Electron session bootstrap singleton, verifying that concurrent image requests share one `fromPartition` initialization, proxy configuration, and `closeAllConnections` cleanup. Also covers the recovery path when CDN session setup fails, making this a useful entry point for Kick image/session partition initialization and single-flight coordination.

Regression test for `kickClient.fetchImageBytes`, ensuring image downloads still reach the network boundary even when platform health is false so `kick-image://` requests do not 404-latch avatars and thumbnails in the UI. Search this file for the health-gate bypass, image fetch contract, and the private `electronRequestBinary` seam used to prove the fix.

Broad Kick client tests for request/auth behavior, covering app-token vs user-token headers, degraded-platform cooldown handling, auth failure reporting, and recovery-probe retry logic around the official API proxy. This is the main test surface for Kick backend client transport, token management, and platform-health integration.

Vitest coverage for the Kick public profile reader, focused on identity resolution, follow-state lookup, and cache reset behavior. Tests the official `kickClient` path versus the first-party fallback, plus edge cases like renamed accounts, null avatars, mismatched IDs, and concurrent reads for profile/follow data.

Vitest tests for the Kick authenticated chat-send window integration and web API helpers. Verifies bearer-token lifecycle, secure JSON escaping in generated browser IIFEs, request headers and payloads, response classification for success/auth/rate-limit/network errors, and viewer-role or moderation-related helpers.

Vitest coverage for Kick live-stream playback resolution, testing HLS URL discovery, channel normalization, offline and missing-URL errors, retry behavior, memory-cache reuse and forced refresh, Electron networking, and privacy-safe timing logs. Helps find tests for Kick stream startup and playback URL caching.

Vitest coverage for Kick moderation mutations: banning, timing out, unbanning, deleting chat messages, and changing chat mode. Verifies official API versus legacy endpoint selection, URL encoding, HTTP methods, request bodies, authorization headers, fallback behavior, and failure handling.

Semaphore tests for the Kick request-slot scheduler used to cap concurrent outbound Kick requests at four. This file exists to validate queueing, release handoff, and in-flight accounting so higher-level Kick API calls do not overload the service or violate throttling assumptions.

Tests for Kick pin and unpin mutations routed through the web-session helper instead of renderer OAuth fetch, with assertions on the `/api/v2/channels/{slug}/pinned-message` payload shape. It also verifies auth-error classification for the UI layer, including unauthenticated, forbidden, and not-found outcomes.

Vitest suite for reading the latest Kick prediction from `/api/v2/channels/{slug}/predictions/latest`, covering anonymous-first fetches, optional bearer-token retry on 401, and parsing of both wrapped `{ data: ... }` and direct response shapes. It also guards the no-prediction cases, slug encoding, and network/error classification used by the Kick integration.

Vitest coverage for Kick moderation timeout authority, validating moderator and broadcaster authorization, exact actor and target identity checks, invalid target states, unverifiable reader failures, timeout policy limits, minute-based durations, and execution payload mapping. Helps locate tests for production Kick timeout safety and moderation permissions.

Vitest regression tests for transforming Kick followed-channel API records into UnifiedChannel objects. Covers stable broadcaster identity, nested and flat response shapes, slug-only identity bridging, missing avatars, live-state defaults, numeric ID coercion, and invalid-row null handling.

Integration-style Vitest coverage for Kick channel and full-search behavior, including public API requests, query variants, deduplication, fallback handling, cancellation, parallel work, live hydration, banned-channel classification, and active-account detection. Mocks Electron networking and related endpoint modules to verify search orchestration without real platform calls.

Vitest coverage for Kick stream endpoint circuit-open behavior under degraded platform health. Exercises stale-cache serving, probe-vs-shed request flow, cooldown timing, and the no-network guarantee for shed requests in `getPublicStreamBySlug` plus the test-only circuit reset helper.

Regression tests for Kick stream discovery and live-status handling across official bulk APIs, legacy fallbacks, caches, throttling, abortable stagger delays, timeout recovery, thumbnail and viewer-count reconciliation, and offline evidence. Exercises network-health reporting and Electron fetch mocks to protect followed-stream polling and playback metadata behavior.

Vitest coverage for Kick user endpoint behavior, including authenticated versus app-token requests, repeated user ID query parameters, deduplication, 50-ID batching, response filtering, null/error handling, profile enrichment, and Electron-backed public channel profile lookup. Mocks Electron BrowserWindow, Kick authentication, browser slot limits, platform health, and logging to verify resilient user and profile retrieval.

Vitest coverage for Kick VOD and video endpoint mapping, pagination, canonical share URLs, metadata normalization, malformed response handling, and completed-stream end-time detection. Exercises Electron network fetch mocking and fail-closed rules for live, missing, invalid, or untrusted timestamps used by offline-channel and last-live logic.

Tests Twitch category endpoint helpers for top categories, lookup by ID, batched ID fetches, and full pagination across pages. Covers cursor propagation, query parameter construction, and the 5000-item safety cap used by `getTopCategories`, `getCategoryById`, `getCategoriesByIds`, and `getAllTopCategories`.

Vitest suite for Twitch channel lookup by broadcaster ID, verifying channel/user merge logic, avatar fallback, empty-input behavior, and the 100-ID guardrail. Good search terms are `getChannelsById`, Twitch channel hydration, and broadcaster/user request parameter mapping.

Minimal tests for Twitch channel chat history retrieval, focused on early return for empty login and graceful null fallback when the Electron network call fails. Useful when searching for `getTwitchChannelHistory`, chat history fetch failure handling, or network short-circuit behavior.

Vitest coverage for Twitch clip discovery by broadcaster and game, verifying query construction for pagination, cursors, time ranges, default page size, and native game IDs. Confirms raw Twitch clip payloads are preserved and cursors are returned only for full pages.

Vitest suite for the Twitch EventSub health bridge that debounces disconnects and records platform health transitions. It verifies reconnect blips, sustained net-error failures, error-state handling, and unsubscribe cleanup around `attachEventSubHealthBridge` and `EVENTSUB_DISCONNECT_DEBOUNCE_MS`.
Empty Twitch GraphQL chat replay fixture with a video node whose comments edges are empty and `hasNextPage` is false. Used to test the no-results path for chat replay pagination and replay parsing.

Synthetic Twitch chat replay page fixture containing one comment edge with cursor, message fragments, badges, and commenter metadata. It supports tests that parse GraphQL chat replay pages, emotes, and pagination cursors.

Twitch chat replay fixture that includes a GraphQL `errors` array and a `comments: null` payload for an expired or transient failure case. It is used to exercise fallback handling when chat replay data is unavailable.
Minimal Twitch chat replay fixture where the video node is null, representing an unsupported or unavailable replay source. Tests use it to validate the parser's unsupported-content branch.

Documentation for the Twitch chat replay fixture set, explaining that the JSON shapes mirror observed Twitch GraphQL responses while redacting identifiers and syntheticizing text. It points developers to provenance notes for the captured response shapes and feature limits.

Tests for Twitch search endpoint adapters that transform raw Helix responses into unified channel and category models. They verify query-string construction, pagination cursors, live-only filtering, default page size, and box-art URL resizing in `searchChannels` and `searchCategories`.

Vitest suite for Twitch stream endpoint wrappers covering user-based stream lookup, followed streams, top streams, and direct login search. It checks request parameter wiring, cursor propagation, stream transformation, verified-status mapping, avatar enrichment, and authentication/error edge cases.

Vitest contract tests for Twitch chat replay fetching and parsing by video ID, playback offset, and cursor. Covers normalized messages, sender metadata, badges, content fragments, pagination, empty or unsupported videos, authentication/rate-limit/transient failures, anonymous requests, and abort propagation.

Unit tests for the Twitch client facade that wrap GQL and Helix endpoint fallbacks, with coverage for platform identity, stream lookup, top-stream pagination mapping, and error-tolerant delegation. This file is the place to find Twitch client behavior around endpoint normalization, fallback strategy, and registry integration.

Vitest coverage for the Twitch EventSub WebSocket client, using mock WebSocket and fetch implementations to test session handshakes, subscriptions, reconnects, notifications, revocations, cleanup, client reuse, POST failures, and orphan subscription deletion. Searches for EventSub lifecycle, WebSocket reconnect, Helix subscription management, and Twitch event dispatch tests.

Vitest tests for Twitch GraphQL client helpers covering game, stream, channel, category, clip, video, VOD, playback-token, follower, search, and live-status queries. Verifies request bodies and headers, response normalization, malformed or missing data handling, network errors, logging, and platform-health reporting.

Tests the Twitch Helix chat pin mutation helpers `pinChatMessage`, `updatePinnedChatMessage`, and `unpinChatMessage`, with emphasis on the `/helix/chat/pins` wire format. It checks HTTP methods, query parameters, auth/client headers, and error classification such as missing scopes, forbidden, not-found, and conflict states.

Vitest tests for the Twitch Helix banned-users API wrapper, including exact-user filtering, pagination, bounded page sizes, authentication headers, malformed payload validation, timestamp parsing, empty responses, and categorized errors for unauthorized, forbidden, not-found, rate-limited, and network failures. Searches for moderation bans, banned-users endpoint, Zod validation, and BannedUsersFetchError behavior.

Vitest coverage for the Twitch Helix `GET /chat/settings` client, focusing on request shape, response parsing, and error classification. It pins broadcaster_id query params, Authorization and Client-Id headers, optional viewer vs moderator fields, and the `ok/kind` result contract used by the shared room-state layer.

Wire-contract tests for Twitch Helix moderation mutation helpers such as ban, timeout, unban, clear chat, warnings, raids, shield mode, commercials, and moderator/VIP changes. The file exists to lock down URL paths, HTTP methods, query parameters, and request bodies so moderator UI actions do not break on field renames or envelope drift.

Tests for `getModeratedChannels` and `getModeratedChannelsResult`, the Twitch Helix `/moderation/channels` fetcher and its result-state wrapper. It verifies pagination cursor following, authorization-failure handling, empty/null-body fallbacks, and a 50-page safety cap that prevents infinite loops in the moderated-channels lookup flow.

Vitest coverage for Twitch Helix moderator and VIP roster queries. Verifies exact-user filtering, broadcaster_id and pagination parameters, response parsing, malformed payload rejection, and missing-scope or forbidden error mapping used by Twitch moderation APIs.

Vitest tests for Twitch Helix poll helpers, covering `getPolls`, `createPoll`, `terminatePoll`, and `archivePoll` with strict assertions on URL, HTTP method, request body shape, and validation rules. It protects the polling workflow in the Twitch backend API by checking title, choice count, choice length, duration bounds, and status enum behavior.

Vitest coverage for Twitch Helix prediction helpers, exercising `getPredictions`, `createPrediction`, `lockPrediction`, `resolvePrediction`, and `cancelPrediction` with request-body and endpoint assertions. It also locks down validation and scope-error handling for the predictions flow, including prediction_window bounds, outcome requirements, and winning_outcome_id resolution.

Vitest coverage for Twitch Helix unban-request CRUD helpers, focusing on list and resolve flows, query-string construction, pagination, scope-missing errors, forbidden responses, and rate-limit handling. The tests pin the request contract for `getUnbanRequests` and `resolveUnbanRequest` so the backend wrapper keeps using the expected Helix endpoint, status filter, and optional `resolution_text` mutation behavior.

Vitest suite for the Twitch public profile reader that resolves public identity, follow relationship, avatar URL, and account-created metadata from Helix and first-party GraphQL fallbacks. It verifies scope gating, reconnect-required behavior, schema-drift protection, and the preference order between official Helix data and validated fallback data.

Vitest coverage for the Electron-main TwitchRequestor HTTP wrapper. Tests main-owned OAuth credentials, authentication failures, token refresh on 401, rate-limit handling, retryable server and network errors with exponential backoff, non-retryable failures, and request method/body forwarding.

Vitest coverage for the TwitchStreamResolver playback URL flow, including live stream HLS URLs, VOD playback, clip quality selection, custom clip media URL encoding, and error propagation from Twitch GQL token fetches. Search this file for resolver behavior around `getStreamPlaybackUrl`, `getVodPlaybackUrl`, `getClipPlaybackUrl`, signed URL construction, and logging guards.

Vitest coverage for Twitch timeout target-state authority checks. Verifies that exact Helix ban, timeout, and moderator reads classify targets as invalid or clear, while malformed, failed, incomplete, or identity-mismatched responses fail closed as unverifiable before timeout actions.

Unit tests for Twitch data transformers that normalize Twitch API stream, game, channel, and search-channel payloads into unified app models. Look here for field-mapping expectations, thumbnail and box-art URL template replacement, and edge cases like missing tags, empty IDs, and partner/verified flags.

Vitest coverage for Twitch user and follow endpoints, including `getUser`, `getUsersById`, `getUsersByLogin`, `getFollowedChannels`, `getAllFollowedChannels`, and `getFollowerCounts`. The tests focus on query-string construction, input limits, pagination, auth gating, API response mapping, and follow-channel enrichment against the Twitch requestor layer.

Vitest coverage for Twitch video endpoint helpers, including user/game video retrieval, single-video lookup, query parameter forwarding, pagination cursor rules, default page size, and raw API data preservation. Uses a mocked TwitchRequestor to validate Helix request construction and response handling.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/api/unified/p.summary: State-machine tests for the unified platform health tracker, validating healthy-to-degraded transitions, rolling-window failure aggregation, listener notifications, and per-platform isolation for Kick and Twitch. The suite documents the outage detection thresholds and recovery boundaries used by the platform-health subsystem.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/api/unified/s.summary: Vitest coverage for the unified slot-controller main-process API, focusing on slot lifecycle, focus-singleton presence rules, max-slot cap enforcement, event fan-out, and crash/retry behavior. Useful search terms: `createSlot`, `destroySlot`, `setSlotPresence`, `getFocusedSlotId`, `dispatchLoadStream`, `onSlotEvent`, and `WebContentsView` test mocks.

Tests the `createSlotHost` wrapper that binds a single slot to slot-controller and forwards host dispatch methods through the slot id. This file is the place to find routing tests for `loadStream`, `setMute`, `setQuality`, `setBufferConfig`, `unload`, and host teardown no-op behavior.

Pure-function tests for the slot crash recovery policy, verifying the rolling retry window and the silent-retry versus user-facing affordance decision. Search here for `decideSlotRetryOutcome`, `SLOT_RETRY_WINDOW_MS`, boundary conditions, and crash-threshold logic.

Vitest coverage for status-page polling across Twitch and Kick, including health-transition start/stop behavior, incident classification, service/component filtering, retry/backoff handling, and safe parsing of malformed responses. Mocks platform-health signals, fetch, timers, listeners, and logging to verify outage detection without warning spam.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/api/unified/w.summary: Tests the injectable WebContentsView factory used by the unified backend API. Verifies the default Electron construction path sets secure webPreferences like sandbox, contextIsolation, and nodeIntegration:false, forwards an optional preload path, and supports swapping/resetting the factory so slot-controller tests can avoid spinning up Chromium.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/auth-hea.summary: Unit tests for the HEADER_RENDERED_PREDICATE string used by the auth window to detect when the login page has rendered. Evaluates the predicate against DOM snippets for both anonymous sign-in and logged-in avatar/menu headers, and confirms it stays false before the auth header appears.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/auth-win.summary: Covers the auth-window manager that opens and tracks Electron OAuth windows for Twitch and Kick. Exercises PKCE/state/redirect URI generation, direct vs. landing-page loading behavior, session lookup, state validation, and safe cleanup of open or destroyed auth windows.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/device-c.summary: Vitest coverage for Twitch OAuth device-code authentication, testing device-code requests, response validation, activation URL safety, error parsing, polling, token normalization, scopes, timers, and authorization status handling. Mocks fetch, OAuth configuration, logging, and managed intervals to exercise the device-code flow deterministically.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/kick-aut.summary: Vitest suite for the Kick auth service covering token lifecycle, stored-user state, scope validation, refresh deduplication, and session-expired cleanup. It exercises `kickAuthService` against mocked storage, cookies, and token exchange behavior so developers can find the OAuth/session management logic for Kick login and refresh flows.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/oauth-ca.summary: Integration-style tests for the local OAuth callback server used by Twitch and Kick sign-in flows. It verifies redirect URI generation, callback parsing, error handling, timeout behavior, and duplicate callback handling around `oauthCallbackServer`.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/oauth-co.summary: Vitest regression tests for OAuth platform configuration and authorization URL generation for Twitch and Kick. Pins worker endpoint overrides, canonical scope sets, IRC chat scopes, channel-management permissions, removed AutoMod scopes, Kick moderation/event scopes, and Twitch consent behavior to prevent authentication and feature-scope drift.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/protocol.summary: Vitest coverage for the Electron deep-link protocol handler used by Twitch and Kick OAuth callbacks. Tests URL parsing, callback registration, malformed or unknown links, protocol registration, and second-instance window restoration and forwarding.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/token-ex.summary: Integration-style tests for `tokenExchangeService.getTokenStatus`, comparing Twitch `/validate` behavior against Kick token introspection and current-user lookup. It verifies how the service derives validity, scopes, user identity, and expiry from provider-specific APIs, making it the place to find token validation and auth status logic.

Vitest coverage for OAuth authorization-code exchange and token response parsing across Twitch and Kick. Verifies PKCE request construction, HTTP and malformed-response errors, scope normalization and defaults, expiry timestamps, and refresh-related error behavior.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/token-st.summary: Vitest coverage for the `AUTH_TOKEN_STATUS` IPC handler that reports Twitch/Kick token state back to the renderer. The tests verify connected vs disconnected responses, token validation flow, sender-origin allowlisting, and that no access/refresh token values cross the IPC boundary.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/twitch-a.summary: Deterministic tests for Twitch authentication token refresh orchestration using mocked storage and token-exchange services. Covers permanent versus transient refresh failures, exponential retry backoff, proactive scheduling, scope preservation and validation, token persistence, and signed-out/auth-lost handling.

Vitest coverage for TwitchAuthService authentication state, token expiry, scope validation, refresh, remote validation, access-token retrieval, and auth-loss handling. Mocks storage, OAuth token exchange, configuration, timers, and Twitch user data to exercise reconnect and proactive refresh behavior.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/ipc/handlers/.summary: Vitest coverage for `registerAdBlockHandlers`, the Electron IPC wiring for adblock status, toggles, stats, cosmetic injection, Twitch proxy controls, and VAFT pattern updates. The tests verify channel registration plus the handler contracts that connect renderer IPC requests to `networkAdBlockService`, `cosmeticInjectionService`, `twitchManifestProxy`, and `vaftPatternService`.

Tests the app-level IPC handler registration and the `APP_GET_ENVIRONMENT` response shape, including dev-mode detection, platform, app version, and runtime versions from `process.versions`. This file is the contract for startup/environment metadata exposed to the renderer through Electron `ipcMain.handle`.

Vitest tests for authentication IPC workflows covering legacy Twitch-token invalidation, Twitch device-code login and popup lifecycle, account persistence, proactive refresh, and post-login follow synchronization for Twitch and Kick. Verifies authoritative snapshot pruning while preventing transient fetch or authentication failures from clearing existing followed-channel data.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/auth/twitch-f.summary: Vitest tests for TwitchFollowWriteCredentialService, covering credential reuse and validation, device-code activation polling, cancellation when the authorization window closes, terminal OAuth errors, scope encoding, storage, and concurrent requests sharing one activation flow.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/context-menu..summary: Tests the pure context-menu template builder used by the Electron backend to decide whether Copy and Paste roles should appear from selection/editability state. Look here for Electron context-menu logic, whitespace selection handling, and the `buildContextMenuTemplate` helper.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/dev-relay/dev.summary: Covers the development media proxy that validates allowed Twitch/Kick CDN URLs, rewrites nested HLS playlist resources through a same-origin relay, and blocks SSRF-style redirects and oversized Range/Content-Length responses. Search this file for HLS playlist rewriting, CDN allowlists, and `buildDevMediaProxyUrl` / `handleDevMediaProxyRequest` behavior.

Verifies the runtime gate that starts the configured development relay only for unpackaged browser development and passes through the expected port, token, and origin. Useful for finding environment-driven dev-server startup logic in `startConfiguredDevRelay`.

Integration tests for the dev relay WebSocket server, covering upgrade authorization, exact origin/token checks, host vs browser roles, and browser-peer replacement semantics. Search here for relay security, rebinding defenses, and the `startDevRelayServer` / `authorizeDevRelayUpgrade` handshake.

apps/desktop/tests/backend/ipc/handlers/.summary: Vitest coverage for the bug-report IPC registration and write flow, exercising `registerBugReportHandlers` against mocked Electron `ipcMain`, `shell`, and log paths. The tests verify the handler wiring plus markdown bug-report generation, directory creation, log tail inclusion, and the fallback path when the noise logger is not initialized.

Vitest coverage for category IPC handlers that load, search, identify, and fetch metadata for Twitch and Kick categories. Verifies IPC registration, bounded versus exhaustive catalog requests, in-flight request deduplication, concurrent multi-platform loading, pagination, partial provider results, and unified discovery responses.

Integration-style IPC tests for channel lookup handlers across Twitch and Kick using isolated databases and mocked platform clients. Covers response envelopes, platform routing, authentication fallbacks, stale-follow recovery by stable channel ID, renamed-channel metadata repair, Kick identity preservation, suspension evidence, and safe cached-follow removal.

Vitest coverage for the desktop main-process chat IPC layer, including Twitch/Kick history handlers, Twitch badge-catalog loading, and mention-enrichment registration. Searches for this file would likely be about Electron `ipcMain.handle` wiring, badge catalog fetch order, request validation, and error-to-`{ success: false }` translation.

Vitest coverage for Chat Replay Electron IPC registration and request handling. Verifies replay load/cancel channels, malformed payload rejection, service bypass on invalid input, and AbortSignal cancellation for in-flight Twitch or YouTube replay windows.

Comprehensive Vitest coverage for download queue IPC handlers and their service delegation. Tests channel registration, clip/video download workflows, queue controls, retries, cancellation precedence, completed-file actions, and renderer-origin security checks.

Vitest coverage for third-party emote IPC handlers spanning 7TV, BTTV, FFZ, and Kick integrations. Verifies channel registration, verbatim service-result forwarding, request parameter mapping, and preservation of null sentinels for missing users, rooms, or emote data.

Vitest coverage for the modlog IPC handler registration and request flow in the desktop backend. Exercises `registerModLogHandlers` across insert/query/retention channels, including moderator authorization checks, origin gating, and coverage-state responses such as `complete`, `partial`, and `verified-empty` from the database service.

Vitest suite for the Kick chat IPC bridge, verifying `registerKickChatHandlers` wires each `ipcMain.handle` channel to the correct backend action. Covers send message, moderation actions, viewer role lookup, and send-window lifecycle, so developers searching for Kick chat IPC or Electron handler registration can find the routing contract quickly.

Vitest coverage for local caption IPC handlers, exercising model state, download/cancel/remove, session start/stop, and audio push flows. The file documents the typed bridge between renderer and the local caption model store/supervisor, including the no-path safety rule and the verified-model startup gate.

Vitest suite for log IPC handlers, validating renderer-to-main log writes, sender-origin checks, and log path queries for main/noise/network logs. It also checks registration of `ipcMain.on` and `ipcMain.handle` channels, making it the place to find the logging IPC contract and security filter behavior.

apps/desktop/.prettierrc.json.summary: Prettier formatting rules for the Electron desktop app, including line width, indentation, quote style, semicolons, trailing commas, and LF line endings. Used by format and format-check scripts across source files.

apps/desktop/eslint.config.mjs.summary: Provides the desktop app's flat ESLint configuration for JavaScript, TypeScript, React, React Hooks, tests, configuration files, and audio worklet globals. Establishes recommended rules, unused-import warnings, TypeScript overrides, ignored build output, and Prettier compatibility.

apps/desktop/src/backend/api/platforms/t.summary: Writes Twitch follow and unfollow actions through Twitch’s persisted GraphQL operations. Exports the follow mutation function and typed authorization/transient error handling for OAuth failures, rate limits, timeouts, and retryable server errors.

Command-driven Twitch API service that translates shared TwitchApiCommand operations into Helix requests for emotes, users, moderation, chat settings, polls, predictions, bans, and related channel management. Exports the TwitchApiService contract and createTwitchApiService factory, centralizing query construction and normalized success/error results for backend callers.

apps/desktop/src/backend/auth/twitch-dev.summary: Secure Electron BrowserWindow manager for Twitch device or activation authorization. Validates Twitch verification URLs, restricts navigation to approved Twitch and callback origins, blocks webviews, popups, permissions, and unsafe redirects, and exports the reusable twitchDeviceAuthWindow manager.

apps/desktop/src/backend/ipc/handlers/co.summary: Registers the Electron IPC endpoint for checking internet reachability. Bridges the connectivity service to Electron's network fetch implementation through the shared connectivity channel.

apps/desktop/src/backend/ipc/handlers/tw.summary: Electron IPC boundary for Twitch API commands, including emotes, users, moderation, chat settings, polls, predictions, raids, commercials, and message management. Uses discriminated-union Zod validation and sender authorization before delegating commands to Twitch API and EventSub services.

apps/desktop/src/backend/services/captio.summary: Normalizes persisted caption preferences into the current platform-caption format while validating BCP-47 languages, model IDs, display sizing, and opacity ranges. It also detects legacy local-caption settings and represents them as unavailable selections without attempting model downloads.

apps/desktop/src/backend/services/chat/s.summary: WebSocket client for 7TV cosmetic events tied to Twitch channels, including badge and paint creation plus user entitlement updates and removals. Exports SevenTvCosmeticsClient, SevenTvCosmeticEvent, and parseSevenTvCosmeticFrame for reconnecting, heartbeat supervision, payload validation, and conversion into shared cosmetic models.

apps/desktop/src/backend/services/connec.summary: Small, injectable internet reachability check used to determine whether end-to-end connectivity is available. Probes fallback no-content endpoints with timeout, no-cache, and redirect rejection, returning a ConnectivityCheckResult for IPC or connection-state consumers.

apps/desktop/src/backend/services/downlo.summary: Validates renderer-provided media URLs before downloads, restricting sources to HTTPS Kick or playback.live-video.net hosts and expected HLS/MP4 paths. Exports assertAllowedRendererMediaUrl, which rejects Twitch renderer URLs, credentials, ports, untrusted hosts, and invalid media extensions.

apps/desktop/src/backend/services/twitch.summary: Manages lifecycle of Twitch EventSub channel-moderation feeds, including token validation, subscription setup, connection-state callbacks, and per-feed cleanup. Exports the feed service interface, factory, and configured singleton used by backend consumers.

Executes authenticated Twitch follow and unfollow actions, validates account credentials, refreshes authoritative followed channels, synchronizes local storage, and confirms the requested state. Exports TwitchFollowWriteService, its factory, and the configured service singleton for follow mutations.

apps/desktop/src/backend/startup/start-p.summary: Small startup policy module that enforces Electron single-instance behavior. Exports dependency interfaces and starts pre-ready setup plus the ready lifecycle only for the primary instance, exiting duplicate launches.

apps/desktop/src/backend/startup/startup.summary: Defines the beginning-of-session policy for clean-shutdown diagnostics. Warns when the prior session lacked a shutdown marker, preserves Chromium cache, and marks the current session as started.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/chat-di.summary: Normalizes persisted chat display settings by merging partial or missing preference snapshots with default values. Provides resolveChatDisplayPreferences for backward-compatible preference loading.

apps/desktop/src/components/chat/ChatCom.summary: Provides the fixed visual container for chat composer controls, including top-border styling, background, spacing, and test identification. Accepts arbitrary React children so input actions and buttons can share a consistent footer layout.

apps/desktop/src/components/download-dup.summary: Alert dialog that asks whether to download a video VOD or clip again when the item already exists in Downloads. Reads pending duplicate state from the download confirmation store, resolves user decisions, and focuses Cancel for safe keyboard behavior.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/hooks.summary: Hook that watches network recovery events and retries player recovery when an active playback error exists, ensuring each recovery notification is handled only once. Exports usePlayerNetworkRecovery and connects player errors to the shared network-status hook.

Pointer and mouse interaction hook for video progress bars, converting horizontal coordinates into clamped playback times and seekable live/VOD ranges with hover previews. Exports useProgressScrubbing with refs, hover state, click seeking, pointer scrubbing, cancellation, and duplicate-commit protection.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/persi.summary: Provides React context infrastructure for registering and sharing the active docked live-player configuration across the desktop app. Exports PersistentPlayerShell plus hooks for reading configuration and registering cleanup-safe player state.

apps/desktop/src/components/player/quali.summary: Converts persisted video-quality preferences into the best matching available quality level and maps selected quality levels back to preference values. Handles auto, source/highest quality, named resolutions, missing height metadata, bitrate, dimensions, and frame-rate tie-breaking.

apps/desktop/src/components/settings/cha.summary: Provides deterministic inline SVG fallback artwork for chat settings previews when third-party emote or badge assets are unavailable. Exports provider-specific 7TV, BetterTTV, and FrankerFaceZ preview emotes, cosmetic badges, and overlay artwork.

apps/desktop/src/components/recording/st.summary: Starts a recording for a playable stream after prompting for capture quality, and displays active recording status with pause/resume and stop controls when recording the current channel. Handles blocked concurrent recordings through ActiveRecordingDialog and formats recording phase and captured duration for the player UI.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/loading-s.summary: Storybook coverage for the LoadingSpinner component, including configurable size and color controls, size comparisons, and Twitch/Kick platform-specific spinner variants.

Reusable animated CSS loading spinner with small, medium, and large sizes plus custom color support. Exports LoadingSpinner and Twitch/Kick branded convenience components for platform-aware loading states.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/platform-.summary: Storybook scenarios for PlatformAvatar, demonstrating Twitch/Kick platform borders, live status dots or badges, missing-image initials fallback, and neutral styling without platform decoration.

Channel avatar component that combines proxied remote images, initials fallback, Twitch/Kick identity borders, configurable sizing, and live indicators rendered as dots or LIVE badges. Used wherever channel artwork needs platform context and resilient image loading.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/progress..summary: Storybook stories for the Radix-based Progress component, providing an interactive value playground, download progress states from queued to complete, and a compact playback-progress variant.

Thin wrapper around Radix UI Progress that applies project theme styling and translates the numeric value into an animated indicator transform. Exports the forwardRef-compatible Progress component for download, playback, and other completion states.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/proxied-i.summary: Storybook coverage for ProxiedImage, showing loaded remote-style artwork, missing-source fallback, custom fallback content, and avatar cropping. Documents the shared image boundary used for Electron-proxied Kick and Twitch assets.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/twitch-ad-fra.summary: Development diagnostic panel that mounts a Twitch live player in an isolated proof fixture and verifies that a clean video frame appears before a timeout. Exports the panel controller, diagnostic and snapshot types, and mount function with render-error, window-error, rejection, and cleanup handling.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/proxied-i.summary: React image component for remote CDN assets, routing Kick and Twitch URLs through custom protocols that handle hotlink protection and broken per-user images. Exports ProxiedImage and a test reset helper, with lazy loading, cache-hit detection, layout dimensions, fallback initials, and session-level broken-URL suppression.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/scroll-ar.summary: Storybook demonstrations for the ScrollArea UI primitive, showing live channel lists and compact metadata layouts with scrolling, truncation, dividers, and status indicators. Exports Storybook metadata plus ChannelList and CompactMetadata stories.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/moderation-br.summary: Development-only contract and response router for browser moderation fixtures selected through the moderationFixture query parameter. Exports fixture types, selection logic, and mocked timeout snapshot/submission responses covering history, errors, reconnects, pending states, failures, and successes.

apps/desktop/src/dev-relay/twitch-ad-fra.summary: Lazy-loads and mounts the Twitch ad-frame proof panel, translating module import or mount failures into structured diagnostics and removing partial DOM state. Exports bootstrap diagnostic types and startTwitchAdFrameProof for development proof runs.

Creates the Vite development proxy configuration for Twitch ad-frame proof runs when the serve command, development mode, and STREAMFUSION_TWITCH_AD_FRAME_PROOF run ID are present. Exports validation and configuration logic that rewrites proof-prefixed paths to a local service at 127.0.0.1:18765.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/mod-log-query-key.summary: Defines typed TanStack Query key factories for moderation log data, including global and platform/channel-scoped keys. Search here for mod-log cache identity and query invalidation patterns.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/network-status-st.summary: Implements an external network connectivity store with browser online/offline events, active reachability probes, single-flight checks, retry backoff, countdown state, recovery tracking, and debug overrides. Exports the store factory, snapshot/status types, and the app-level networkStatusStore consumed by reactive UI hooks.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/queries/useLiveFa.summary: Combines favorite channels from the multistream store with per-channel React Query lookups and returns only currently live streams. Exposes a normalized result with live stream data, aggregate loading state, and the first query error.

apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-share-action..summary: React hook for safely copying verified public Twitch and Kick clip or video URLs to the clipboard when playback is ready. Validates supported HTTPS URL formats, tracks copied state per content identity, resets feedback with a managed timeout, and displays toast results.

apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-density-presen.summary: Maps compact, cozy, and loose chat density settings to reusable Tailwind row, line-height, and padding classes. Used by chat message components to keep density-specific presentation consistent.
